articleTitle: Formation of Use Case Scenario Based on Use Case Diagram Using Text Semantics for IdVar4CL Application Development
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In forming a Use Case Scenario, alignment is needed between two artefacts, the Requirement Elicitation and the Use Case Diagram, so the software development meets the client's needs. There is a process for forming a Use Case Scenario that can be inconsistent with the Use Case Diagram. This inconsistency can occur due to differences in the interpretation of an artefact and a lack of validity and reliability between the software developer and the client's needs in representing it in a Use Case Diagram. This research aims to create a Use Case Scenario using a semantic text process based on a Use Case Diagram. After completing all stages of this research process, four main points emerged as results: ten Use Case Names accompanied by Use Case Diagrams with similar names, tabulation of the Use Case Scenario format, which is the result of the formation of related artefacts, the alignment of the Use Case Scenario formed based on the Use Case Diagram produces a comparison value of 0.39 “fair agreement” and a value of 0.75 “substantial agreement”, and references that produce artefact improvements related to the Requirement Specification documentation for the formation of the Use Case Scenario. The results of this research are expected to help developers enhance development and documentation, making it more effective in consistently meeting user needs.

articleTitle: Downlink Throughput, SINR & Coverage Analysis in Urban Scenario for LTE & mmWave 5G NR MIMO
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: 5G New Radio (NR) is a global standard for 5G wireless air interface as it provides more responsive and faster mobile experiences. Calculating 5G NR throughput and Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) helps network operators evaluate the effectiveness of their network design, configuration, and optimization. The urban scenario is one of the five deployment scenarios established by the 3GPP that use mmWave technology. A Wireless InSite, Wireless propagation simulation study was undertaken to estimate the effect of precoding schemes at 5G MIMO, BS and various diversity combining techniques at the UE in presence of multipath interactions and scatterers in Urban Scenario. When compared to LTE, SISO at 1.8 GHz, beamforming in a mmWave 5G NR cellular network at 28 GHz improves downlink throughput by more than 6 times. SINR and coverage for LTE network was higher than mmWave 5G which improved significantly with large array gains of MIMO system and beamforming coming relatively close to LTE. Best network performance for the defined user distribution was achievable with combination of MRT precoding at BS with Maximum Ratio Combining (MRC) at UE

articleTitle: An Improved Modified Adaptive PNGV Model for Electric Vehicle Battery Performance and Charge Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: EV battery modeling improves energy economy, performance, safety, lifespan, and environmental friendliness. Misestimating State of Charge (SoC), heat management, deterioration prediction, and dynamic load fluctuations are EV battery modeling issues. For these issues, this research provides a modified Adaptative Partnership for a New Generation of Vehicles (m-PNGV) LiFePO4 battery model. The m-APNGV model improves EV battery performance through temperature management, power loss control, and SoC stability. Simulation using MATLAB/Simulink evaluates the proposed m-APNGV equivalent circuit model for a LiFePO4 battery. Battery management efficiency and accuracy are shown by the model. The proposed m-APNGV model outperforms the Thevenin model (TM) for all battery properties in a comparison of the two LiFePO4 battery circuit models. The thermal behavior, temperature measurement accuracy, polarization resistance, power loss, open circuit voltage, and SoC stability during discharge are significantly evaluate using the proposed m-APNGV model, ensuring enhanced battery performance and reliability under dynamic operating conditions.

articleTitle: Automated Attendee Recognition System for Large-Scale Social Events or Conference Gathering
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Manual attendance tracking at large-scale events, such as marriage functions or conferences, is often inefficient and prone to human error. To address this challenge, we propose an automated, cloud-based attendance tracking system that uses cameras mounted at the entrance and exit gates. The mounted cameras continuously capture video and send the video data to cloud services to perform real-time face detection and recognition. Unlike existing solutions, our system accurately identifies attendees even when they are not looking directly at the camera, allowing natural movements, such as looking around or talking while walking. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first system to achieve high recognition rates under such dynamic conditions. Our system demonstrates overall 90% accuracy, with each video frame processed in 5 seconds, ensuring real-time operation without frame loss. In addition, notifications are sent promptly to security personnel within the same latency. This system achieves 100% accuracy for individuals without facial obstructions and successfully recognizes all attendees appearing within the camera's field of view, providing a robust solution for attendee recognition in large-scale social events.

articleTitle: Blockchain Beyond Cryptocurrency: Exploring the Revolutionary Potential of Decentralized Ledgers in Supply Chain Management, Healthcare, and Governance
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research aims to identify the possibilities that can be harnessed in supply chain management, healthcare, and governance in light of blockchain technology. In doing so, we examined the effectiveness, transparency, and security of the above sectors through the use of blockchain systems. In supply chain management integration, it was established that Blockchain leads to savings of up to 75% of the transaction time and 87%. This approach would lead to a 5 per cent error reduction rate, thus improving operational transparency and audibility. In the health industry, Blockchain has made access to records faster by 75%, while security malfunctions have been brought down to 93%. 3%, and at the same time, the level of user satisfaction was raised by 35%. 7%. In governance, the blockchain voting systems eradicated voting inaccuracy by voting accuracy of 100%, system failures by 80%, and enhanced voter confidence by 38%. 5%. Hence, comparative analysis with the data available in the literature also establishes these findings and proves that the blockchain solution outperforms a traditional system. Thus, based on the identified strengths and weaknesses, it is possible to state that Blockchain has significant advantages that can contribute to the development of innovation in different fields and has only specific issues connected with its implementation and security. Thus, the present study highlights the effectiveness of the Blockchain in the practical application of the mentioned fields and its potential to address the most significant problems in these industries.

articleTitle: Automated Nuclei Segmentation Using Shearlet Based Unsharp Masking
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Accurate nuclei segmentation is essential in pathology since evaluations and diagnoses are mostly dependent on the measurement, identification, and counting of nuclei. Automated segmentation in digital pathology is a difficult task due to several factors, including, hazy nucleus boundaries, low contrast between nuclei and background, varying nuclei sizes and shapes, and imaging modalities. In this work, a new nuclei segmentation method is proposed which incorporates the shearlet-based unsharp masking (SBUM) technique to pre-process the source images together with the CNN-based U-Net architecture. The SBUM method primarily enhances the source image's high-frequency details. The effectiveness of a developed nuclei segmentation technique is compared to the existing techniques using a common dataset. The developed method achieves IOU, Accuracy, F1Score, and Precision values as 0.8146, 95.93%, 0.8953, and 0.8725 respectively. The empirical findings demonstrate that the developed method outperforms the existing methods.

articleTitle: Multiplexer SRAM Combination-Based Design of Multiple Combinational Gates for In-Memory Computation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Traditional computing systems based on the Von Neumann architecture face challenges with speed and power consumption. To address this, SRAM is used for fast memory access while minimizing power usage. In-memory computation (IMC) leverages SRAM to perform basic computations, such as NAND and NOR, directly within the memory, improving throughput and reducing power consumption. However, IMC adds area overhead due to the integration of computation within the memory. This paper presents a novel design for NAND, NOR, XOR, and Half Adder (HA) for IMC, implemented using 18nm Fin-FET technology, offering better performance with less area overhead than previous methods.

articleTitle: A Novel Neuro Fuzzy Deep Random Vector Functional Link Network for Early Cancer Diagnosis Using Thermography
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Breast cancer ranks among the most prevalent cancers impacting women globally. Regular screening plays a crucial role in early detection, helping to lower risks and improve survival outcomes. While mammography is a widely adopted screening tool, its limitations such as exposure to radiation, reduced sensitivity in dense breast tissues, and high costs necessitate exploring alternatives. Thermography is a non-invasive and radiation free medical imaging technique that measures heat patterns on the surface of the skin, to detect abnormalities that indicate the presence of breast cancer. Despite the advantages, its effectiveness is often limited by subjective interpretations and low sensitivity in detecting small or deeply located tumors. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a neuro fuzzy deep random vector functional link network for early detection of cancer from thermal images. The architecture is designed for fast training and adaptability, with the fuzzy layer enhancing both interpretability and robustness. Together, they create a hybrid model that effectively balances accuracy, computational efficiency, and the ability to manage imprecise data. With performance metrics of 96.44% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, and 98% specificity, the model demonstrates significant potential as a superior alternative for breast cancer screening. By integrating interpretability with advanced learning capabilities, the model contributes significantly to the growing field of AI-driven diagnostic tools, offering a promising solution to a pressing global health challenge.

articleTitle: Stuttering Detection Using LSTM and LSTM-Attention Based Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Stuttering is a common speech disorder which results in involuntary repetitions, prolongations, blocks or interjections while speaking. Detection and evaluation using traditional methods is time-consuming. Therefore, we conduct a study on 2 classification based deep learning models for stuttering detection: 1) a model which comprises of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) followed by Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Attention layers 2) a model which comprises of a CNN followed by LSTM layer only. We used the SEP-28K dataset for training and evaluating our models. These models take mel spectrogram as input and perform binary classification for each disfluency label of the SEP-28K dataset. The CNN + LSTM + Attention model achieved a higher accuracy of 70.47% in detecting prolongation, 60.80% in block and 56.90% in word repetition compared to the CNN + LSTM model, which achieved 69.43%, 60.34% and 55.23% for the same labels, respectively. However, the CNN + LSTM model outdid the attention-based model in classifying fluent/no-stutter instances with 66.52% accuracy against 61.50% and sound repetition with 65.22% accuracy against 64.25%. For interjection, both the models had similar performance in terms of accuracy. For F1 scores, the CNN + LSTM + Attention model showed improvement in block, prolongation, sound and word repetition classifications, while the CNN + LSTM model observed better results for fluent/no-stutter and interjection detection.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Cost-Effective 3D-Printed Cylindrical Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A cylindrical Luneburg lens with a gradient-index (GRIN) profile focuses electromagnetic waves by gradually reducing the refractive index (RI) from center to edge. However, conventional designs face challenges such as complex fabrication, material limitations, narrow bandwidth, and high costs. This study introduces a 3D-printed Luneburg lens with saw-tooth structures that achieve a smooth RI gradient through unit cells with cuboidal and cylindrical air voids, precisely tuning permittivity. With a diameter of 95.9 mm, a height of 30 mm, and operation in the X-band, the lens achieves a simulated gain of 14.07 dBi. In contrast, measured gains for cuboidal and cylindrical designs are 11.91 dBi and 12.85 dBi, respectively. This method offers a low-cost, high-performance alternative for GRIN lenses.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization Glass/AZO/Ag Ultraviolet Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this article, we demonstrate the succinct report on Al-doped Zinc Oxide (AZO) and pristine Zinc Oxide (ZnO) based ultraviolet photodetector device fabrication on the glass substrate. Pristine Zinc oxide (ZnO) and Al-doped ZnO (AZO) nanoparticles were prepared using a simple chemical sol-gel route. The prepared ZnO and Al-doped ZnO (AZO) nanoparticles have been characterized using XRD, and high-resolution SEM for phase formation, and surface morphology respectively. XRD graph confirmed the formation of the wurtzite hexagonal structure of ZnO. The device performance was measured using a semiconductor parametric analyzer with a UV light source for -2V to 2V.

articleTitle: Adaptive Logistic Regression: Leveraging Arctan in Active Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Creating labeled data for supervised learning can frequently be expensive and time-consuming, which makes it difficult to train efficient models. By selectively querying the most informative data points for labeling, active learning provides a strategy that lowers the quantity of labeled data needed while preserving model performance. In this work, a method for incorporating the Arctan function into logistic regression for active learning scenarios is presented. The logistic regression model's stability and resilience are improved by utilizing the Arctan function, which has a smooth and gentle transition between probability limits, especially when working with sparsely labeled data. Our approach aims to improve the efficiency of model training in situations where labeled data is scarce. Through a series of simulations, we demonstrate that the Arctan-based logistic regression model also achieves high accuracy in terms of convergence speed and generalization capability. The results indicate that this method is a promising alternative for applications where data labeling is a bottleneck, offering a more efficient and effective solution for supervised learning tasks. This research contributes to the ongoing exploration of alternative activation functions in machine learning and their potential to improve model performance in challenging scenarios.

articleTitle: Compressor-Based Approach for Power-Optimized Error-Tolerant High Accurate Approximate Multipliers Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A common operation in many different applications is multiplication. The performance of a multiplier can be increased by using compressors. Approximate multipliers fall under Approximate Computing, a developing approach focused on en-hancing power efficiency, reducing area, and minimizing delay in applications that can tolerate acceptable errors. It also trades off the necessity of exact computation for improved performance. By using this approach, power usage can be reduced in applications in which precision is not given much importance. An efficient 8-bit approximate multiplier design is achieved by introducing a approximate compressor. The experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in an 8-bit multiplier, reducing total power by up to 28.4% versus exact multipliers and 31.71% versus existing designs while decreasing delay by up to 54.93% and 72.15% respectively. The average accuracy is found to be 97.02%. The results not only reduce the power consumption but also maintain acceptable levels of precision, demonstrating that this is an effective solution for modern image processing and signal processing applications. The findings add to what we already know about approximate computing, which is important for future research and development in creating energy-efficient digital systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Resource Utilization of Big Data in Healthcare for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Big data in healthcare involves gathering, analysing, and interpreting vast amounts of medical information, such as electronic health records (EHR), diagnostic images, and real-time sensor data from wearable devices. With the growing volume of healthcare data, there is an increasing demand for sophisticated machine learning models that can process this data and extract meaningful insights. One of the most important uses of healthcare big data is predicting cardiac diseases, where early and accurate diagnoses can significantly enhance patient outcomes. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with attention mechanisms, known for their ability to process sequential time-series data, are particularly effective in analyzing dynamic signals like ECGs and heart rate data. The attention mechanism improves the LSTM's ability to focus on the most relevant parts of the input data, thus boosting model performance, especially in handling complex sequences. This study introduces an LSTM with Attention Mechanism model that surpasses traditional machine learning algorithms in classifying cardiac diseases, yielding higher precision and recall. These findings highlight the value of LSTM with attention mechanisms in enhancing the accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability of predictive models for cardiovascular diseases, providing a scalable solution for real-time, data-driven healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis and Unsupervised Clustering of Faults in Grid-Connected Solar PV Systems Using K-Means
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper conducts a statistical analysis of seven faults that impact a gridconnected solar power plant using the K-means clustering algorithm for unsupervised data categorization. The clustering reveals distinct fault patterns, aiding in precise fault detection and system maintenance. Our findings emphasize the combined effectivenessof statistical and machine learning techniques in enhancing the reliability and efficiency of SPV (solar photovoltaic) systems, promoting sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Integrating Facial Image Data for Autism Identification: A Comparative Evaluation of Deep Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by difficulties in social relations, communication, and behavior, and as was shown by the results of several studies, deep learning models may be used for automated diagnosis of subjects with this disorder. This study aims to explore how deep learning models can be used to classify images of autistic individuals' facial features. For this purpose's objectives, a comparative analysis through several deep learning classifiers namely VGG16, VGG19, VGG Faces, and Resnet50 was performed to assess their ability to classify images of faces of children. The dataset includes 2926 images and the balance between autistic and non-autistic people was maintained. To improve model performance and to counter overfitting, we performed some preprocessing operations such as image normalization and resizing and used some data augmentation techniques such as rotation, shearing, and flipping. The results showed that the ResNet50 model accounted for all other models' limitations and achieved the highest score of 97.14%. The results of the study are linked to the recruitment of deep learning tools for the detection of ASD providing a great hope for improved tools for earlier interventions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Low Power Leakage-Controlled SRAM Cell
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Since the dawn of the 21st century, the rise of IoT-powered portable devices has sparked a revolution in low-power SRAM development. As the complexity of such devices has exponentially increased to support a higher number of operations, advanced power management techniques are now essential to minimize power consumption. Consequently, low-power circuit design continues to be a prominent area of research. This paper introduces an innovative low-power SRAM cell design that surpasses traditional options. Compared to conventional 6T SRAM and DTMOS-based SRAM cells, simulations demonstrate that the proposed design significantly reduces power consumption without compromising propagation delay, marking a promising advancement in SRAM technology. The simulations were conducted using the Siemens Tanner EDA Tool version 2022.2. The supply voltage and operating frequency were set to 2V and 100MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Classification of 3D Dynamic Contrast Enhanced Breast Tumour MRI Images Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Breast cancer remains the most prevalent malignant tumor in women worldwide and a significant contributor to female mortality. Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) is an emerging technique for the diagnosis of breast disease, and it is highly efficient in the recognition, observation, and diagnosis of tumors. Additionally, there is hope that more advanced applications for early breast cancer diagnosis may be developed by recent advances in image processing and deep learning. In our study, a 3D CNN deep learning tool was designed to classify breast tumors into stages of malignancy in contrast to prior works that generally classify images as benign or malignant. Firstly, the 3D DCE-MRI images are preprocessed and then split into training and validation sets. The train set was augmented, and combined data was fed into 3D CNN, which provided 81% training accuracy and 71% validation accuracy. Further work, a prediction application program interface was created using our pretrained model in which the stages for each of the 3D images loaded were predicted. The hypothesized 3D CNN model has shown good accuracy in classifying the four distinct stages of breast tumors, namely stage 1, stage 2, stage 3, and stage 4. This can aid radiologists in making more accurate predictions and in the early diagnosis of breast tumors.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a 16-Channel DWDM RoF System Using 112 Gbps Coherent DP-QPSK Modulation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Development of DWDM-based RoF Technology was prompted by the growing needs for high data rates and huge channel capacities. With the use of appropriate dispersion compensation methods & digital modulation techniques, system performance efficiency can be further improved and upgraded. We had suggested 112 Gbps data rate per channel RoF communication system with 16 channel capacity with DWDM technology. In the given system direct modulation technique with DP-QPSK digital modulator is used and for dispersion effect fiber Bragg grating compensator is employed. This analysis of system is being carried out inOptisystem16.0 for the transmission range of upto 350 Km for spacing of channel ranging from 25 GHz to 100 GHz. The execution of proposed system is observed in terms of different performance metrics constellation diagram, SNR& Power spectrum obtained for different channel. We had obtained optimum power output in the range of (24–25 dBm) for the give system design with different channel spacing, laser input power and for varying transmission range. Also with the use of FBG nonlinearity and dispersion effects gets reduced.

articleTitle: Enhanced Image Steganography Using Customized Differences between the Neighboring Pixels
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the digital era, safeguarding sensitive information from unauthorized access is paramount. Image steganography, which inconspicuously embeds data into visual media, has emerged as a promising solution. However, balancing data embedding capacity with image quality remains a challenge. This study introduces a novel steganographic method that optimizes visual fidelity and payload capacity by utilizing customized differences between neighboring pixels within grouped blocks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of up to 48.99 dB and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) as low as 1.20 on complex images like “Baboon.” Additionally, Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) values consistently reach a perfect 1.00 across several test cases. The method also achieves a significant payload increase, embedding up to 119,496 bits in the “Resolution Chart” image. By leveraging the precise control over pixel differences, this study introduces a new paradigm in steganography, addressing the trade-off between capacity and quality while ensuring imperceptibility and high efficiency.

articleTitle: Highly Birefringent Terahertz PCF Using Epsilon-Near-Zero (ENZ) Material for Polarization Maintaining Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: We propose an innovative triangular lattice photonic crystal fiber (PCF) in terahertz (THz) that incorporates gain doping and epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) material to attain elevated birefringence and linear polarization. The selective filling of four holes with ENZ material in cladding's first ring, while leaving the other two as air-filled, results in an asymmetrical material and structural configuration. The considerable loss of ENZ material establishes a notable disparity in loss between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>-polarized, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>-polarized, and other higher-order modes. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>-polarized mode exhibits a marginally greater field distribution in the ENZ material, thereby permitting only the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>-polarized mode to realistically persist in PCF after a brief propagation distance. The incorporation of doped gain material in core slots effectively mitigates losses in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>-polarized mode due to ENZ while maintaining the existing loss differential. This proposed PCF demonstrates a significant value of 0.6201 in birefringence, prominent differential loss of ~ 11.4 dB/cm, and 0.2 THz of Linear-Polarization Single-Mode (LPSM) bandwidth between 1.3 and 1.5 THz. This PCF seems to be the most significant birefringent photonic crystal fiber showcasing an extensive LPSM bandwidth documented in the THz range. These attributes enable this PCF to be critical for their applications in polarization-sensitive THz filters, modulators, and sensors.

articleTitle: Binarization in DeepFake Audio Detection: A Comparative Study and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: DeepFake audio, generated through advanced AI techniques, poses significant risks such as fraud, misinformation, and identity theft. As the quality of synthetic audio improves, detecting such fakes has become increasingly challenging. Traditional detection methods struggle to keep pace as AI-generated voices replicate speech patterns, tone, and pitch convincingly. While computationally intensive large-scale models can help detect DeepFakes generated by AI, their resource requirements make them impractical for deployment on mobile devices as well as on resource-constrained devices. This paper proposes a lightweight yet effective approach using binarized neural networks (BNNs) and further enhancements using additional dense layers and stacked modeling to overcome these challenges. We conduct a comprehensive performance analysis of the network and compare it with various machine learning and neural network methods to evaluate the tradeoff between detection accuracy and computational efficiency as an effect of binarization and precision loss in feature embeddings.

articleTitle: Decentralized Security Architecture for Health IoT Leveraging TGA and ANN
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Rapid adoption of Health Internet of Things (Health IoT) revolutionized healthcare by enabling continuous monitoring and real-time data analysis. However, the massive influx of data generated by Health IoT devices presents significant challenges in data processing, security, and efficient task management. This paper proposes a novel Task Group Aggregation-Based Overflow Handling with Artificial Neural Networks (TGA-ANN) framework utilizing Fog Computing to enhance security and efficiency in Health IoT systems. The TGA-ANN framework leverages TGA to manage and prioritize data tasks effectively, preventing overflow and ensuring timely processing. By integrating ANN within the fog layer, the framework enhances decision-making capabilities, enabling intelligent task distribution and anomaly detection to bolster security. This approach mitigates the risk of data breaches and unauthorized access, ensuring confidentiality and integrity sensitive health information. The obtained results demonstrate that the TGA-ANN framework significantly improves data processing efficiency, reduces latency, and enhances security measures compared to traditional cloud-based solutions. This research provides robust and scalable solution managing growing demands Health IoT, paving the way for more secure and efficient healthcare services.

articleTitle: A Printed E-Shaped Monopole Patch Antenna for ISM Band-I (2.4 GHz) & 6G Communication (7–20 GHz)
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Upcoming generation of communication (6G) provides data transmission at high speed with lower latencies. In this paper a dual band microstrip patch antenna has been designed applicable for ISM-I (Industrial Scientific and Medical) band and future communication 6G. An E-shaped patch structure with partial ground has been developed using FR4 substrate (εr = 4.4). Antenna is operating from 2.3 GHz to 2.5 GHz with center frequency of 2.4 GHz. The first band provides a bandwidth of 200 MHz and another band is operating from 7 GHz to 20 GHz with bandwidth of 13 GHz. At first band overall gain of 4 dBi is observed while at second operating band overall gain lies between 5 to 6 dBi. Radiation efficiency (η) at first band of 94% and at another band it lies between 68 to 90% with average efficiency of 74<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. All simulation process has been performed on HFSS 2024 student version.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of IRS-Assisted Communication Systems Under Rayleigh Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a key enabling technology that helps in modifying the propagation environment. In this paper, we investigate the performance of an optimized IRS based communication system in the presence of single eavesdropper considering Rayleigh fading. It is assumed that the channel state information (CSI) of the transmitter-to-IRS's and IRS-to-receiver's channels is perfectly known to the IRS. The simulation results demonstrate that proposed optimized IRS based communication system has a noticeable performance improvement as compared to the random IRS based communication system in terms of channel capacity and secrecy capacity. Furthermore, our results show secrecy performance improvement with increase in number of IRS reflecting elements.

articleTitle: Intelligent Human Behaviour Detection Leveraging ConvLSTM and LRCN Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research delves into intelligent human behavior detection from video sequences by employing advanced deep learning methodologies. The study harnesses the capabilities of Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) and Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Networks (LRCN) architectures, which are adept at capturing both temporal and spatial dynamics in video data. Using the extensive Kinetics dataset, which includes a wide range of human activities and contexts, the video data was converted into sequential image frames for model training. The ConvLSTM and LRCN models were implemented and trained with the TensorFlow/Keras framework on GPU-accelerated systems. During training, both models exhibited effective learning, with improved accuracy and reduced loss. However, validation metrics revealed fluctuations, indicating possible overfitting and challenges in generalizing to new data. To address these issues, regularization techniques such as dropout and early stopping were applied, alongside comprehensive hyperparameter tuning. Additionally, the study investigated the use of transfer learning to enhance model performance. This research lays the groundwork for sophisticated video-based human behavior detection systems, with applications in surveillance, healthcare, and human-computer interaction. Future work will aim to bolster model robustness and broaden the scope of action recognition.

Author Keywords: Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Convolutional Network LRCN

articleTitle: Intelligent Malware Detection Using Sentence Transformer and Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The complex evasion techniques adopted by the malware creator make signature-based malware detection approaches unable to detect unknown malware attacks. This study proposes a new malware detection and classification approach with significantly less dependence on manual feature engineering. The bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) are used to model the opcode sequences of the malware file as the semantic behavior of malware. After that, the vectorized feature vector is fed to the hybrid one-dimensional convolution neural network (1D-CNN) and the gated recurrent unit (GRU) model for feature reduction and normalization before training a Softmax classifier. A hybrid learning architecture is designed with a custom 1D-CNN and a GRU model to take the strengths of both types of networks. The proposed scheme is evaluated using the Microsoft BIG dataset, consisting of 1625 assembly files belonging to 9 distinct malware families. The proposed method produced 95.77% accuracy even with the smaller dataset, which we believe will boost performance by adding a more diverse dataset. It uses the next-generation BERT language model, which gives a promising future area for malware defenders. This research presents malware detection without much reliance on manual feature engineering or signature-based detection, making it suitable for detecting unknown malware attacks.

articleTitle: HMSIW-Based MIMO Antenna with Enhanced Isolation for Advanced V2X Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a 2-port Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna based on Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) is proposed. The antenna consists of modified L-shaped slots on the top metallic plane of the HMSIW structure. The antenna achieved a high port isolation of 35 dB and a significant gain of 4.86 dBi. These performance characteristics are attained with an electrical size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.23\lambda_{0}\times 0.52 \lambda_0$</tex>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> represents the free space wavelength at the resonant frequency. Specifically, the antenna operates at 5.57 GHz, corresponding to 5G NR bands n46 and n47, which are well-suited for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications, meeting the requirements for reliable and high-speed data exchange in V2X applications. Additionally, the MIMO antenna exhibits a mean effective gain (MEG) of -3 dB, diversity Gain (DG) of 9.99 and envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) of 0.000071. The proposed HMSIW-based MIMO antenna, with its advantages such as compact size, high isolation, and efficient performance, is particularly suitable for advanced V2X applications.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Biquadratic Fractional Order Filter Using VDTA
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel configuration for a biquadratic filter employing a single voltage differencing transconductance amplifier (VDTA) and fractional order capacitors. The proposed filter leverages the flexibility and tunability of VDTAs in conjunction with fractional-order components to achieve enhanced performance and control over frequency characteristics. Fractional capacitance elements, modelled using Continued Fraction Expansion (CFE), are implemented to enable the realization of fractional-order impedance, allowing for smoother transitions and improved selectivity compared to conventional integer-order filters. The proposed design is validated through LT SPICE simulations utilizing TSMC CMOS technology. Key parameters such as fractional order and cutoff frequency are studied to demonstrate the adaptability of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Assessment of a Metal-Strip on Stack Gate Oxide Underlap TFET for Improvement of Analog/RF and Linearity Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The work presented in this article investigates the effectiveness of presence of low work function live metal strip in improving the performance in terms of analog/RF and linearity parameters for Live-Strip-Dual-Material Gate-Oxide-Stack Double-Gate TFET (LWLS-DMGOSDG TFET) as compared to conventional DMGOSDG TFET under the influence of underlap of 5nm towards the source end. The analog/RF and linearity Figure of Merits (FoMs) such as transconductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(g_{m})$</tex>, gate-to-source and gate-to-drain capacitances, gain-bandwidth product (GBP), cut-off frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{T})$</tex>, second and third order transconductances, Input Intercept Point (IIP3), Voltage Intercept Point (VIP3) and intermodulation distortion (IMD3) have been considered during the device simulation. The simulation results approve the applicability of the proposed device for low power applications.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Fraud Identification in International Shipping
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: With a surge in global trade between several countries, there has been a high rise in fraud cases involving the wrong declaration of goods by domestic parties. Traditionally, random inspections are done by customs officers, and the finding of fraud is often by chance. To alleviate this challenge, an intelligent data-driven machine learning (ML) model must identify frauds efficiently. In this paper, we design and develop a simple ML model to identify frauds effectively. We use shipment data comprising several features used during the custom declaration. We investigate the fraud identification for different possible feature combinations. Moreover, we also compare our model with different ML models. Results demonstrate that with all features combined, the ML model based on the Isolation Forest outperforms. This signifies that fraudsters can be easily identified through customs officers' inspection of domestic parties.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Sensitivity Analysis of GaAs/GaSb Heterojunction Polarity-Controlled TFET for Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Dielectrically modulated heterostructure tunnel field effect transistor (TFET)-based biosensors have emerged as promising solutions for low-power, ultra-sensitive detection of bioanalytes. This paper introduces a GaAs/GaSb heterojunction polarity-controlled TFET (GaAs/GaSb HJ-PC-TFET) biosensor for label-free detection of biomolecules, employing a heteromaterial and a polarity control approach to enhance sensitivity and reduce fabrication complexity. The polarity control technique is used to form the p+ source regions, avoiding challenges associated with ultra-sharp doping concentration gradients, high thermal requirements, and complex fabrication processes. The sensing capabilities of the GaAs/GaSb HJ-PC-TFET biosensor is evaluated based on variations in drain current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{DS}})$</tex> in response to different biomolecules. To assess its performance, biomolecules with dielectric constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k)$</tex> ranging from 1 to 24 were examined. With a k-value of 24 for a neutral biomolecule, the proposed GaAs/GaSb HJ-PC-TFET biosensor has an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{DS}}$</tex> sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.52 \times 10^{13}$</tex>. Higher sensitivity indicates, the GaAs/GaSb HJ-PC-TFET biosensor is a highly promising device for advanced biosensing applications.
