articleTitle: Wearable Triple Band Dual Polarization Antenna for Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to wearable Multiband dual-polarized antenna, providing crucial mechanical adaptability for wearable devices. The proposed wearable triple band antenna, with dimensions measuring 1.5λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 1.8λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 0.02λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>uses a felt substrate with the rectangular patch, utilizing a hexagonal-shaped slot and truncated patch edges for better performance. The proposed design operates in triple bands, providing a -10dB impedance bandwidth across 6% from 2.42 GHz to 2.57 GHz, 2.78% from 5.32 GHz to 5.47 GHz, and 2.75% from 6.95 GHz to 7.1 GHz. Further, the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth ranges from 1.51% from 5.26 GHz to 5.34 GHz and 2.7% from 6.91 GHz to 7.1 GHz. The antenna achieves a maximum realized gain of 5.3 dBi, 3.2 dBi, and 10.5 dBi at frequencies of 2.5 GHz, 5.4 GHz, and 7 GHz respectively. The proposed antenna supports both linear polarization and right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) with high gain and finds potential applications in wearable communication systems like ISM and IOT devices.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Object Detection Accuracy in Diverse Background Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Object detection models must perform effectively across diverse environmental conditions to support autonomous navigation and surveillance systems. YOLOv5 and MobileNetV2 were evaluated using a custom dataset of 100,000 images captured under varied conditions, including daylight, fog, rain, and nighttime. YOLOv5 achieved an F1 score of 0.89 and a precision of 0.91 in low-light and rainy scenarios, demonstrating robustness in challenging environments. MobileNetV2 delivered faster inference speeds of up to 45 FPS on devices like the Raspberry Pi 5 and Google Coral Dev Board, with an F1 score of 0.82 in clear and foggy conditions, making it a strong candidate for resource-constrained deployments. The evaluation highlights YOLOv5's advanced feature extraction for high-accuracy detection and MobileNetV2's lightweight architecture for computational efficiency. These findings enable informed decision-making when selecting models for edge-based object detection applications, particularly in cost-sensitive and real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dopingless TFETs with SiGe Heterojunctions: A Reliability Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel heterojunction design for a dopant-less tunneling field-effect transistor (DL-TFET) aimed at enhancing the on-state current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{on})$</tex> while addressing the challenge of forming an abrupt tunneling junction without doping. The proposed approach utilizes a silicon-germanium (SiGe) layer to replace silicon in the source region, thereby sharpening the tunneling junction at the source/channel (S/C) interface and significantly improving charge carrier tunneling efficiency. Additionally, the device's reliability was analyzed considering the impact of trapped charges at the silicon dioxide interface. Simulation results demonstrate that the SiGe-based heterostructure DL-TFET offers an efficient and reliable solution for low-power applications in next-generation electronic devices.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Dielectric Modulated Dual Gate Gallium Nitride Junctionless Accumulation Mode Nanowire FET Based Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study investigates the Dielectric Modulated Dual Metal Gate Gallium Nitride Junctionless Accumulation Mode Nanowire FET (DM-DG-GaN-JAM-NWFET) as a potential biosensor for applications in the biomedical field. To assess its sensing capabilities, neutral and charged biomolecules are analyzed, focusing on the effects of different dielectric constants and charge densities on the device's electrostatic properties. Key parameters, including threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) and on-current (Ion) are examined to evaluate the sensitivity of device. Additionally, the performance of the Dual Metal Gate Gallium Nitride Junctionless Accumulation Mode (DG-GaN-JAM) Nanowire FET is compared with that of the Single Metal Gate Gallium Nitride Junctionless Accumulation Mode (SG-GaN-JAM) Nanowire FET. The results highlight that the DM-DG-GaN-JAM-NWFET biosensor is highly effective for biosensing applications.

articleTitle: Latch and Flip-Flop Design Using Memristors and Transmission Gates with Timer Counter Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Memristors are a combination of the words Memory and Resistor, it never forgets. It is a passive element which remembers the amount of current that flowed through it and is small in size. All these qualities of a memristor make it highly advantageous and useful in the upcoming times for chip manufacturing and designing. Latches are sequential circuits using them in master-slave configuration a flip flop can be generated which is highly useful in applications such as counters, registers, etc. In this paper we implement a Modified version of D-latch and flip flop using memristors and Transmission gates to improve the switching speed and to obtain full voltage swing. Further we show a comparative analysis of proposed modified D-latch and flip-flop with an earlier method along with a timer counter as an application of the D-flip flop circuit. Paper also explains the challenges of using MRL gates in complex circuits. TEAM model of memristor and 180nm technology node files are used in simulation of all the circuits using Cadence Virtuoso.

articleTitle: Study of RSSI and Throughput in Identical Residential Units with Various Wi-Fi Configurations
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Indoor communication is very popular in residential and office environment for the users with low mobility. Wireless signals are significantly affected by various obstructing materials and surfaces. This paper presents a study measuring the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) and throughput in a typical 3BHK residential unit. The propagation scenarios are line-of-sight (LoS), obstructed LoS (OLoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS). The operating frequency band of transmitted wireless signal is sub 6GHz band. We placed some more obstructing material inside the flat and analyzed the receiver performance in terms of RSSI and Throughput. The study observed a relationship between RSSI and throughput across different propagation scenarios and found that, in some cases, the performance under OLoS conditions was superior to that of LoS.

articleTitle: Probe Based SIW Microwave Sensor for Detection of Adulteration in Mustard Oil
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A low-cost Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based sensor is proposed in the paper for detection of adulteration of edible oil especially mustard oil. The adulteration in mustard oil is done in variety of ways by adding low cost oil in different percentage of volume by volume. These adulterations produce multiple health hazards to the human mankind as the edible is used in daily consumption at Indian homes. The proposed sensor is based on probe techniques, where the detection of dielectric constant change is measured by dipping the one end of sensor in the liquid and may be reutilized after cleaning. The change in the dielectric constant of the liquid is expected when there is mixing of any kind oil to the pure mustard oil. This change in dielectric constant produces shift in the S-parameter which is measured through the VNA. The paper proposed a SIW based sensor with concentric rings at the end of the probe to make it sensitive to the small change if dielectric constant of the edible oil changes. The resonance of the probe is fixed to the X-band to make it cost effective due to low cost dielectric material used for fabrication.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive Broadband Absorbing Metasurface Based on Phase Change Material
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: We present in this paper the design and simulation of a broadband terahertz (THz) metasurface (MS) absorber utilizing the phase changing feature of vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The proposed design achieves a 2.41 THz absorption bandwidth, providing over 90% absorption efficiency in the range of 4.27 THz to 6.68 THz under the metallic state of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. On the contrary, VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reverts to its insulating state under thermal control which leads to near complete reflection of the incoming wave. Owing to the balanced design, the absorber offers polarization insensitive absorption. The device under both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarization shows consistent performance with oblique incidence angles up to 40°. The proposed absorber has potential application in various fields such as terahertz switching, modulating and many other futuristic 6G applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of High Speed Cascode Cross-Coupled Stage Comparator in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Low power dynamic comparator is generally used in ultra-low power applications. This device uses ‘28nm CMOS technology’ and the ‘Power Supply Voltage’ is “l.1V”. In order to reduce “Static Power Consumption” and increase comparison ‘Speed’ most dynamic comparators use a pair of cross-coupled inverters as latch level. This provides a decent power input. Here used double tail latch comparator with cross coupled gives the advantages in the power consumption and input referred RMS noise. Unlike traditional architectures, adding cross-connectors to different pairs of inputs prevents end-to-end comparison of nodes. Reducing the overall effect of the stage, the delay of the rate is decided by the total conductance value of the cross-coupled logics of the comparator transistors with a gate-to-source voltage of zero. This work presents a novel low voltage cascode cross-section and high contrast circuit using CMOS technology. The design concept does not use the standard cross-coupled inverter architecture, but uses gate blocking cross-coupled transistors. This concept increases the overall transconductance value at the beginning of the comparison stage, resulting in faster comparison and lower power consumption. Through simulation and measurement, the “Delay” and “Power Consumption” of the compared products are analyzed and compared with previous models. Test results show that the comparator is recommended to be used from a 1.2V power supply with reference voltage 1-2V consumes less energy.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Credit Card Fraud Detection: SHAP and LIME for Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: With the rapid growth of e-commerce and online banking, credit card scams have become a significant challenge. Traditional approaches to detecting scams have been outper-formed by machine learning techniques. However, the understanding behind the classification of transactions as fraud or legitimate is limited. To address this issue, we have implemented two explainable AI (XAI) methods - Local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) across eight machine learning models, which include logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, support vector machine, extreme gradient boost, naive bayes classifier, k-nearest neighbors, and a basic neural network. The results show how individual features of the data set contribute to the decision of a specific prediction. The detailed code for the project is provided here.

articleTitle: Optimised Power-Efficient Design of Approximate Multiplier Using Approximate Compressor
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Approximate computing is a paradigm that aims to trade off computational accuracy for gains in performance, power efficiency, and resource utilization, which is particularly beneficial in Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) design. This approach can be useful in applications where exact precision is not crucial, such as multimedia processing, machine learning, artificial neural networks (ANNs), Error-Tolerant Applications, Emerging technologies like quantum computing and neuromorphic computing. In this paper, we propose an optimised power-efficient approximate multiplier that utilizes precise 4:2 compressors and approximate 4:2 compressors. The compressor has low power consumption, which decreases the overall power usage of the multiplier. The multiplier's functionality was simulated, and the design was then synthesized in Xilinx ISE (Integrated Synthesis Environment) to analyze and verify its power consumption. The proposed Model 1 and Model 2 approximate multipliers significantly decrease power consumption by 68.62% and 72.289% respectively, accuracy by 70.433% for Model 1 and 97.865% for Model 2 when handling higher 8-bit values compared to the exact multiplier. This reduction in power usage is particularly beneficial for power-constrained application and also the proposed approximate multipliers require significantly fewer LUTs (Look-Up Tables) than the exact multiplier. Approx-imate multipliers can be effectively utilized in image processing applications where computational efficiency is crucial and slight errors in calculations can be tolerated.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Hilbert Vibrational Decomposition on Chaos Based Image Encryption Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Image encryption is a crucial technique used to protect the confidentiality of digital images. Advanced encryption techniques are driven by sophisticated mathematical algorithms. In this work, the role of Hilbert vibrational decomposition (HVD) is highlighted for improving the security of existing chaotic map-based image encryption algorithm. The HVD breaks down the input image into its instantaneous amplitude and frequency components, ordered by descending energy levels. These components are then subjected to successive confusion-diffusion process before being reintegrated to produce the final encrypted image. The effect of HVD on security of encrypted image is evaluated through four key parameters i.e. entropy, correlation coefficient of adjacent pixels, NPCR (net pixel change ratio) and UACI (unified average change in intensity) values. The experiment suggests a significant improvement in security by incorporating HVD.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of FinFET Based Baugh-Wooley Multiplier Using PFAL
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Multipliers are crucial components in many computational tasks, with their efficiency being vital in various applications. With the evolution of chip technology, FinFET devices present a promising alternative to traditional bulk CMOS, providing advantages in power efficiency and performance. Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic (PFAL) is another technique aimed at reducing power consumption further. This paper explores the design of the Baugh-Wooley multiplier using PFAL in the context of 18nm FinFET technology, implemented using Cadence Virtuoso Tool. The focus is on understanding the trade-offs between power consumption and performance when integrating PFAL with FinFET technology. While adiabatic logic circuits typically achieve low power dissipation, they often suffer from increased delays.

articleTitle: A Wideband Polarization-Independent Metasurface Absorber Using Vanadium Dioxide (VO2)
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the paper, a tunable wideband terahertz (THz) absorber incorporating a metasurface (MS) structure has been proposed and analyzed. The MS consists of Vanadium dioxide rings as the upper layer, gold (Au) as the bottom layer and silicon dioxide as the dielectric layer in between. The structure exhibits an outstanding absorption bandwidth achieving over 90% absorbance within the range of frequency from 5.52 to 10.88 THz when subjected to normal incidence. Moreover, when the conductivity of Vanadium dioxide changes from 200 to 2e5 S/m, the intensity of the absorption peak can be varied from 3.3 to 99.9%. The structure is also polarization insensitive in nature owing to the fourfold symmetry. It is indicated by the result that the MS absorber maintains of over 90% for incident angles up to 50 degrees under transverse electric (TE) as well as transverse magnetic (TM) polarization. The power loss analysis shows that the top layer consisting of Vanadium dioxide is primarily responsible for absorption. The designed absorber holds great potential in the fields of modulation, imaging, sensing, and switching technology.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensitivity Analysis of Electrically Doped GaSb/GaAs Heterojunction TFET
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work proposes a thorough numerical simulation investigation into the impact of temperature for electrically doped GaSb/GaAs heterojunction TFET. Extensive simulation-based analysis of the temperature variability of DC parameters over a 300–450 K temperature range, including transfer characteristics, sub-threshold swing (SS), and ON state current to OFF state current ratio (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oN</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oFF</inf>) has been demonstrated in this study. A standard EDTFET model and the suggested design are compared with regard to RF performance parameters. The RF/Analog conduct of the proposed design against temperature has also been investigated using the TCAD simulator. In the comparative study, it has been found that the GaSb/GaAs heterojunction TFET proposed here is more resistant to temperature effects than the conventional EDTFETs. This demonstrates that in applications that require low power at severe temperatures, the demonstrated GaSb/GaAs heterojunction TFET, is more reliable than the conventional TFET.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Efficacy of Machine Learning Models Towards Forecasting the Influence Spread of Nodes in Complex Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The identification of influential nodes in social networks is a favoured research area, owing to its use in myriad domains, especially with regards to viral marketing. Centrality measures are the most widely used to assess the influencing capability of nodes, though with the increase in network size the process becomes resource-intensive. In recent times, machine learning (ML) models are also being used to predict the influence spread of nodes, thereby aiding towards the identification of influential nodes. This paper evaluates the efficacy of diverse ML regressor models, employed to forecast the influence potential of the nodes, by taking various features as input vectors in a propagating scenario, under two real-world complex networks. This framework initially generates the feature vectors corresponding to each node using the node's structural and temporal aspects, and infection rates. It employs regression-based ML algorithms to learn the connection between the expected spreading ability of each node and its structural characteristics. Light Gradient Boosting Machine Regressor outperformed the other models with an average mean absolute and mean square error of 0.1232 and 0.1079, respectively.

articleTitle: A Study on Thickness Optimization and Variation in Lead Free Perovskite $\text{CH}_{3}\text{NH}_{3}\text{SnBr}_{3}$
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This research explores the potential of CH3NH3SnBr3 as a lead-free alternative in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) through SCAPS-1D simulations. PSCs have gathered immense attention for their high efficiency and low-cost fabrication, yet concerns regarding the toxicity and stability of lead-based perovskites persist. The device architecture is composed of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ITO}/\text{TiO}_{2}/\text{CH}_{3}\text{NH}_{3}\text{SnBr}_{3}/\text{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O}/\text{Au}$</tex>, where ITO serves as the transparent conductive layer, while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> act as the electron and hole transport layers, respectively. The thickness of the perovskite layer was varied in equal increments from 100 to 1000 nm. increasing the perovskite layer's thickness has the potential to enhance the device's efficiency Furthermore, simulations examined the impact of parameters such as absorber thickness, interface defect density, temperature, and variations in series resistance and shunt resistance on cell performance. The efficiency of conversion for the device is estimated (efficiency)% at higher thickness. the study indicates that CH3NH3SnBr3 perovskite shows promise as a suitable material for future solar energy applications.

articleTitle: Applying the Multifractal Model of Asset Returns (MMAR) to Financial Markets: Insights and Limitations
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study presents an application of fractal mathematics to financial markets through the utilization of the Multifractal Model of Asset Returns (MMAR). The model is employed to analyse a 30-year dataset encompassing three distinct financial markets: the USD/NOK currency pair, the OMXS30 stock index, and the 12-month LIBOR rate. The MMAR model successfully captures essential stylized facts about financial markets, including high kurtosis, non-independent price movements, and clustered volatile days. Simulations generated by the model demonstrate realistic behaviour and multifractal characteristics. However, the model lacks a statistical method for assessing its accuracy and may underestimate kurtosis in high-kurtosis markets. Notably, the model is capable of producing simulations across a wide range of kurtosis values and can be instrumental in stress-testing portfolios. Despite its potential, the model is subject to limitations, such as the need for human judgment, ambiguous predictions, and interpretability issues. Furthermore, the model may become unreliable following a high-kurtosis event.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of a Polarity-Controlled Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor-based Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) is an emerging device for developing highly sensitive biosensors. In this paper, a polarity-controlled TFET (PC-TFET)-based biosensor has been introduced for label-free biomolecule detection. By incorporating the polarity control concept, the biosensor simplifies the fabrication process, minimizes random dopant fluctuations (RDFs), and eliminates the need for high-temperature annealing processes. Additionally, a nano-cavity is created by etching specific areas of the polarity gate's dielectric oxide near the tunneling junction, allowing for better control over the device's tunneling mechanism. The proposed PC-TFET biosensor's sensing capability has been examined for a variety of biomolecules with varying dielectric constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(k)$</tex> and charge densities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\rho)$</tex>. The sensitivity responses have been analyzed in terms of transfer characteristics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{I}_{\text{DS}}-\mathbf{V}_{\text{CG}})$</tex>, subthreshold swing (SS), ON-OFF current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{I}_{\text{ON}}/\mathbf{I}_{\text{OFF}})$</tex> ratio and threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\text{Th}})$</tex>. The suggested PC-TFET biosensor provides excellent sensitivity for both charged and neutral biomolecules.

articleTitle: Optimized Channel Length and Off State Current for InAs/Si Heterojunction TFET
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: this paper contains the Optimization and Comparative study of the Planar Architecture of InAs/Si Heterojunction TFETs. Optimizations performed on the Original Model such as Channel length is reduced to 45nm and Gate Metal overlapping is introduced. Doping concentrations are varied to optimize the electrical device parameter after modifying the physical dimensions of the original model. The Optimized model presented shows some significant improvements such as Reduced off state current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>) while on state current (Ion) remains same and minimum Subthreshold swing slightly increased to 7.3mV/Dec. I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> by I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ratio is about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>. Comparative study with Original Model and other parameters of the optimized model are presented further in the paper.

Author Keywords: Off state Current On state Current Sub-threshold Swing Gate Metal Overlapping

articleTitle: Automated Weed Detection Using YOLOv8: A Deep Learning Approach for Indian Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Weed detection in manual phase is a very hectic and challenging task. People do not have sufficient information about the weed and their types. Numerous weeds are found in the Indian subcontinent and it is very hard to recognize them manually. More difficult task is to remember the names of the weeds. Research done on this field is very limited. So, to full fill the gap for this problem this research has been done to develop a Deep Learning model which can identify the weeds using image processing. It beautifully illustrates the combine usage of the modern technologies and their real-life implementations to make things easy in agricultural field. The technologies such as Image processing and deep learning are used. These technologies blends together to give a good response rate in weed detection. First step is, to collect data from the fields. Secondly data preprocessing and augmentation should be done. Third is classification of the data as training data and testing data and then feed it to yolo v8 library. Dataset of 1000 images of a weed in the ratio 80:20 should be used, 800 for the training of the model and 200 for testing. One can use YOLOv8 python library for training the data and Jupyter Notebook as computing platform. Proposed model can easily get an accuracy around 74 percent.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Interference Limited Hybrid RF/FSO Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The letter investigates the performance of Satellite-terrestrial hybrid radio frequency (RF)/ free space optics (FSO) communication system. In this work, two links are considered to connect the terrestrial node with a Satellite in space. One link follows the RF spectrum which is used as an standby arrangement. The main link is the one where optical link is established through the wireless medium between the ground device and the Satellite. The proposed model also includes the effect of multiple RF interferers operating in the vicinity of the terrestrial node. The RF link has been modeled with the aid of Rician shadowing statistical model whereas the FSO link under-goes atmospheric turbulence with misalignment errors, modeled as Gamma-Gamma distribution. Closed-form expression for the outage probability has been derived in the work considering the impact of interference.

articleTitle: Enhanced Data Hiding Based on First, Middle, and Last Order Pixel in Spatial Domain Images
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet technology has revolutionized global information sharing, enabling faster and more efficient digital communication. However, the increased reliance on online platforms for exchanging sensitive information raises significant concerns about data security, as unauthorized access and misuse of transmitted data pose severe risks, including identity theft and financial fraud. Steganography has emerged as a promising technique for securing data by embedding it imperceptibly into digital media. This study introduces a novel steganographic method that utilizes the difference between pixels in the cover image to embed secret messages while maintaining high image quality. The proposed scheme divides image pixels into blocks of 9. It calculates the difference between pixels with each block's first, middle, or last pixel to ensure minimal distortion and superior visual quality post-embedding. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the method, achieving consistently higher PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) values compared to a baseline approach, with a PSNR of 64.9205 dB for a 10 KB payload and similarly superior results for payloads of 20 KB and 40 KB.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Enhanced Approximate Message Passing for mmWave Massive MIMO Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to channel estimation in millimeter-wave beamspace massive MIMO systems. The proposed method is an approximate message passing algorithm that utilizes a flexible discriminative denoiser. The denoiser consists of two parts: a noise level map identifier and a convolutional neural network. By learning the channel structure and estimating the noise characteristics, the denoiser enhances the performance of the message passing algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed network outperforms networks using DnCNN denoisers and existing compressed sensing-based algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Obstacle Detection and Classification for Visually Impaired Individual
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The article reports an electronic system based on raspberry pi for detection and classification of the obstacles for the blind individuals. The significant electronic module utilized for performing the mentioned function is regulated through the YOLO algorithm. This algorithm on execution yields dual output for intercepted obstacles, namely, the classification of the obstacles and far point and near point of the detection. This two spatial point of the proposed system corresponds to 1209.99 and 3.75 cm, respectively. The detection and classification are experimentally performed for two different obstacles including the cell phone and human body. The experimentally characterized electronic system is proficient to be employed for the application of many fields of engineering and science.

articleTitle: Simulation and Performance Evaluation of RIS Aided Beyond 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this work, we have considered the Re-configurable Intelligent surface (RIS) aided beyong 5G communication systems. The system considered the two scenarios. First, we have taken the scenario where a RIS aided path as well as a direct path are present between the transmitter and the user equipment. In the second scenario, only the RIS aided path is considered as an obstruction present between the transmitter and receiver. The simulation is validated with the theoretical results of the Rayleigh channel model. The BER performance is thoroughly investigated. It has been observed from the results that more reflecting elements on RIS plane improves error performance. The Bit-Error Rate (BER) performances of Binary-Phase-Shift-Keying (B-PSK) and 4-QAM schemes are also evaluated for a comparative study. The free space path loss values are calculated by varying transmitter-receiver separation, and for different carrier-frequencies using urban 5G large scale model.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of FIR Filter Using Different Architectures: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The article proposes a hybrid sparse particle swarm optimization algorithm (HSPSO). This paper also presents an improved low-pass FIR filter design utilizing the HSPSO algorithm. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is contrasted with particle swarm optimization and sparse PSO in resolving the FIR filter design problem. HSPSO offered smaller best cost and execution time values. Furthermore, the suggested approach competes with the existing approaches in the literature, providing higher stopband attenuation values and smaller passband ripple values. The proposed work implemented the designed FIR filters, employing various multiplierless techniques, including the canonical signed digit (CSD) number system, fractional CSD (FCSD), distributed arithmetic (DA), and parallel distributed arithmetic (PDA). The comparative study of all the architectures and multiplier-based structure (MULT) is performed for the FPGA and ASIC environments. The DA outperforms all the architecture in area and power. The PDA with decomposition factor 4 provides the highest throughput and also smaller area and power compared with MULT, CSD, and FCSD-based architecture.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis of RFID Based Authentication Scheme for IoT Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed the way devices or systems interact and function, allowing seamless connectivity and automation in various industries. However, as interconnected devices grow, security and authentication issues become increasingly vital. This article explores the importance of authentication in the security of devices and IoT systems, emphasizing the need for robust and reliable mechanisms to verify the identities and permissions of devices, users, and data within the IoT network. This research presents a cryptanalysis of a highly efficient authentication and key agreement scheme based on the elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman (HAKECC) scheme. The model discovered potential risks such as physical tampering, denial of service (DoS), and tag cloning associated with insecure authentication schemes within the IoT ecosystem. By understanding the critical role of authentication in IoT security, organizations and stakeholders can implement effective measures to safeguard their interconnected devices and systems, mitigating potential threats and vulnerabilities in the IoT landscape.

articleTitle: Wideband and Tunable Terahertz Metamaterial Absorber Using Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, we have presented a unit cell metamaterial structure of rectangular shape based on phase change property of Vanadium dioxide's (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and applicable as wideband tunable terahertz Metamaterial Perfect Absorber (MPA). Here, above 90% absorption is reported with excellent bandwidth of 4.23 THz at VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> conductivity 1.35xl0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> S/m. Output is tunable in 4% to 97.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> range by changing the conductivity with respect to change in temperature. The proposed absorber is polarization insensitive. Permittivity, permeability, impedance, reflection coefficient, and electric field distribution are all thoroughly examined. The investigation validates the destructive interference and impedance matching theories for perfect absorption. The suggested absorber is useful for a wide range of fascinating applications, such as imaging, sensing, and terahertz modulation in wireless communication.

articleTitle: Blockchain Enabled Data Communication Scheme for Vehicular Named Data Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: With the tremendous increase in the number of vehicles they exchange of information among them has also increased specifically aimed at road safety. Mostly, the information traveling in this network is important and personal, which brings security and privacy an important aspect during the information sharing. Here, Named Data Networking emerges as a futuristic network architecture that aims to focus on the content rather than the address of the content. Along with this, it provides in-networking caching, security, and adaptive data forwarding features for proving a Quality of Service (QoS) to the network. However, when this is applied on the vehicles termed as Vehicular Named Data Networking, a lot of challenges arise because of highly mobile vehicles. These challenges specifically raised concern towards the QoS and security aspects. The use of a decentralized ledger is required where every data packet can be sent from a verified vehicle only. This ensures that only authenticated and authorized data sources are contributing in the network, thus preventing malicious attacks. In this paper we have proposed a Blockchain enabled Data communication scheme for Vehicular Named Data Networks (BD-VNDN). This scheme provides an authenticated data packet to every interest packet and has been designed for vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure-based communication. To verify the efficiency of the proposed scheme, extensive simulations have been performed on the ndnSim simulator. Different scenarios have been evaluated for the scheme and the results have been analyzed in terms of such as throughput, interest satisfaction delay, and interest success rate.

articleTitle: Tuning of Piezoelectric Energy Harvester for Self-Powered Pacemaker Application
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper explores the design, simulation, and optimization of a fan-folded piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) for pacemaker applications. The objective of this work is to develop a self-sustaining energy source by capturing mechanical vibrations from human heartbeats, reducing the dependency on traditional batteries. In this study, a five-beam fan-folded PEH structure has been optimized to achieve a resonant frequency below 5 Hz, aligning with the low-frequency range of human physiology using COMSOL 6.2 Multiphysics software.6.2. Through iterative adjustments in beam length, tip mass, and beam thickness, this work successfully reduced the fundamental resonant frequency from 13 Hz to 2 Hz, achieving a more effective frequency match with physiological vibrations. This work underscores the potential of fan-folded PEH designs to enhance pacemaker longevity, reduce battery replacement surgeries, and improve patient quality of life. Future steps include experimental validation to support integration and performance in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Analyzing Trap Charge Impact in Dopant Hetero-Material TFET via Interface Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Enhancing the performance of Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs) requires the formation of a sharp tunneling junction. This challenge is particularly significant in doped-TFETs (D-TFETs). To address this, we propose a novel hetero-dielectric and hetero-junction design for a D-TFET, utilizing silicon-germanium (SiGe) in the source region. The proposed design enables the creation of a sharper tunneling junction at the source/channel (S/C) interface, resulting in a higher tunneling generation rate of charge carriers. Furthermore, device reliability was evaluated under the influence of trapped charges at the oxide interface, demonstrating the potential of the proposed hetero-structure for low-power electronic applications.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch Strategy for Roof Top Solar PV-Based EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV) are exciting alternatives to conventional vehicles (CV) which have zero carbon emission during operation. The electric vehicle's ability is to reduce total climate effect & pollutant emission significantly. In This paper present a comparative analysis study of an optimization dispatch strategy for electric vehicles (ODSEV) charging station by using general algebraic modelling system (GAMS) to solve optimization dispatch equation. In the current distributed electricity generation scenario, a reliable, economical energy distribution plan is required. The problem of pollutant emissions from fossil fuels and their finite supply have forced researchers to concentrate on the future of renewable energy production. The output of this paper is to optimization dispatch strategy for electric vehicles (ODSEV) which includes four thermal & one solar power plant. This paper aims to introduce a cost-effective and environmentally conscious algorithm that integrates both thermal and solar power plants. Additionally, the algorithm accounts for the uncertainties associated with varying climatic conditions, ensuring a more practical and adaptable solution.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Classifier: Performance Enhancement Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Skin cancer ranks among the most prevalent human malignancies, primarily diagnosed through visual methods, commencing with clinical screening, followed by dermoscopic analysis. The intricate alterations in the visual appearance of skin lesions pose a considerable challenge for automated classification through images. Deep learning techniques have been harnessed to support dermatologists in enhancing diagnostic accuracy. To address this, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed to achieve highly discriminating and potentially generalizable results for image classification problems. This research introduces a prediction model designed to classify skin lesions into seven categories using the HAM10000 skin cancer dataset. The MobileNetV2, Resnet50, and DenseNet121 models were used in this study. The MobileNetV2 outperforms with 99.72 % accuracy and achieves 0.88, 0.89, and 0.88 values of precision, recall, and F1 score.

articleTitle: Exploring Circuit Families for Optimizing $3\times 2$ Multiplier: Design and Analyses
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation and analyses of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 2$</tex> multiplier using various circuit families, with the aim of optimizing it for reduced delay, area, and power consumption. A multiplier is one of the most important blocks of many Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) applications operating as an arithmetic combinational logic circuit, also known as the digital multiplier for binary digit multiplication. Through simulations, we explored multiple circuit families including CMOS logic circuit, Pass transistor logic circuit, Transmission gate logic circuit, Pseudo NMOS logic circuit, Cascode Voltage Switch Logic (CVSL) circuit, Clocked CMOS (C2MOS) logic circuit, and Dual Threshold Pass Transistor (DTPT) logic circuit. We have performed Monte Carlo and Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) assessing performance, stability, and reliability of the circuits in terms of power and delay. Additionally, we have focused on other parameters like area, transistors used, and Power-Delay Product (PDP). Comparison of simulation results helped to investigate the effectiveness of different circuits in multiplier optimization. We devised a Novel circuit for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 2$</tex> multiplier by combining elements from various logic families, yielding superior outcomes across the metrics. Our research reports a comprehensive design and analysis of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 2$</tex> multiplier which underscores the thorough optimization of the multiplier, as evidenced by our simulation's outcomes. Notably, our Novel circuit exhibited the least power consumption, moderate delay, and PDP. It gave an optimal balance between transistor count and area utilization. Further, it was observed from the Monte Carlo analyses and PVT analyses that confirmed good stability and reliability of the circuits for real-life conditions. Our study shows the design, analyses, and optimization of the Novel circuit, which outperforms conventional logic circuits in terms of efficiency and robustness.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Based Fusion of CT and MR Images
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for fusing MR and CT images to create a high-contrast fused image that integrates complementary information from both input images. The proposed approach employs wavelet transform to decompose the CT and MR images. Next, features are extracted from the decomposed images by applying transfer learning from the VGG19 model. The fusion of these decomposed images is performed based on the extracted features and the fusion rules outlined in this study. An inverse wavelet transformation is then applied to the fused decomposed images, resulting in a final fused image that encompasses information from both the CT and MR images. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated and compared with five other advanced fusion techniques through both visual assessment and objective measures.

articleTitle: RIWAPV: Robust Image Watermarking in Compressed Domain Based on Adjacent Pixel Variation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The increasing progress of multimedia data in the present digital era necessitates novel solutions for efficient storage and intellectual property protection. This work introduces RIWAPV, an efficient technique that simultaneously achieves image compression and secures digital image ownership verification. Unlike relevant state-of-the-art techniques, the RIWAPV uses a newly developed adjacent pixel variation method for image watermarking. By utilizing the sparse nature of the Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (FWHT), RIWAPV effectively decreases storage requirements while safeguarding ownership rights. The process begins with image compression via FWHT, followed by embedding a chaotically encrypted watermark inside FWHT coefficients. This approach ensures that the imperceptibility of the host image is maintained while enhancing the watermark's robustness. The robustness of this method is demonstrated by high NCC values, consistently close to 1, indicating strong resistance to various attacks. Additionally, the scheme achieves a compression ratio of 2.86, underscoring its efficiency in reducing storage needs. Comparative analysis shows that RIWAPV outperforms several cutting-edge techniques, making it a highly effective solution for the challenges of current digital era.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Sensing Properties of SOI-SDG-FinFET for Chemical Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this study, a chemical-based gas sensor was implemented using a silicon-on-insulator FinFET with a stacked dielectric gate configuration (SOI-SDG-FinFET), employing a conductive organic polymer as the gate material. The polymer gate enhances the sensor's sensitivity to a wide range of chemical analytes, including methanol, iso-propanol, and chloroform. This enhancement is attributed to changes in the work function of the conductive polymer upon exposure to gas vapors, which subsequently modify the electrical characteristics of the proposed device. Furthermore, the temperature dependence of the SOI-SDG-FinFET was analyzed over a range of 250 K to 450 K. The proposed device exhibits a reduced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{OFF}$</tex> current, an improved <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{ON}/I_{OFF}$</tex> ratio, and enhanced sensitivity. These advancements position the SOI-SDG-FinFET with a conductive polymer gate as a promising candidate for applications in chemical and pharmaceutical industries, environmental monitoring, and biological diagnostics.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of High-Sensitivity AlGaN/GaN Based MOS-HEMT Biosensor for Biomolecule Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work reports a simulation and analysis of the electrical properties of the Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor High Electron Mobility Transistor (MOS-HEMT) utilized as a biosensor. A cavity is incorporated on the drain side of the MOS-HEMT for bio-sensing applications. The gate-to-source distance is considered smaller than the gate-to-drain distance to enhance the sensitivity. The impacts of charged and neutral biomolecules on the electrical properties, such as drain current and threshold voltage sensitivity, are thoroughly examined. An increase in the dielectric constant leads to a decrease in the drain current, while an increase in the positive charge of biomolecules increases the drain current. The maximum observed shifts are -3.45 V in threshold voltage and 40.99 mA/mm in drain current for neutral keratin biomolecules. Similarly, for a charged biomolecule with a charge density of 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>, a shift of 0.8 V in threshold voltage and -25 mA/mm in drain current was recorded. The structural analysis of the MOS-HEMT biosensor uses Silvaco ATLAS software, providing insights into its performance in detecting biomolecules.

articleTitle: Sub Threshold Performance Comparison of Doped and H-Cu Carbon Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article focuses on the electrical modelling of the doped and hybrid carbon interconnects that has been implemented by incorporating the scattering effects in the sub threshold domain of operation. Additionally, the circuit's performance in terms of X-talk (crosstalk) has been assessed. This work focuses on detailed comparison of electrical performance of both the hybrid-Copper-Carbon/H-Cu Carbon and lithium (Li) doping based graphene nanoribbon (MLGNR) interconnects in the context of dynamic as well as functional X-talk at sub threshold operating regions employing transmission line (TL) modeling. The grain size impact on copper (Cu) resistivity and different scatterings on the combined mean free path (MFP) influencing the resulting resistance have been demonstrated in the modeling of H-Cu Carbon interconnects. The effectiveness of hybrid interconnects, particularly H-Cu-Carbon interconnects, is ensured by a thorough examination of the normalized X-talk caused delay (dynamic X-talk), the time-duration (functional X-talk) and the normalized +ve peaks.

articleTitle: Assistive System for Monitoring Malnutrition in Children
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Monitoring key health indicators can provide early detection of conditions associated with malnutrition and anemia. This paper presents an automated system for assessing Body Mass Index (BMI) and hemoglobin concentration to enable efficient, non-invasive health monitoring. BMI, calculated from weight and height, is a widely used measure, while anemia -a condition affecting a large segment of the global population -typically requires invasive blood tests. To address this, a novel near-infrared optical method using red and infrared LEDs is employed, based on a redesigned Beer-Lambert law that compensates for light attenuation at nonlocal sites, allowing for hemoglobin estimation without invasive procedures. Integrated with ESP32 microcontrollers, the system includes large-scale weight and height measurement units, which transfer data to an IoT (Internet of Things) cloud and display information on an OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) screen. This low-cost system supports real-time, accessible health monitoring.

articleTitle: Exploring SRAM Layout Using Open-Source Tools: A Case Study with Skywater 130nm PDK, Magic, Xschem, ngSpice, and OpenRAM
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of a 6T SRAM cell design and implementation using a suite of open-source tools, including Magic, OpenRAM, xschem, and ngspice. The research encompasses the complete design flow, from individual component design and simulation (6T SRAM cell, D flip-flop, write driver) to the generation of a 16KB SRAM array layout using OpenRAM. The design is implemented using the Skywater 130nm PDK, ensuring compatibility with industry-standard fabrication processes. Simulation results validate the functionality and performance of the designed components. OpenRAM facilitates the visualization and analysis of the complete memory array, providing insights into layout complexities and the impact of design choices on overall performance. This study underscores the efficacy of opensource tools for accessible and cost-effective SRAM design, paving the way for further innovation in memory system development

articleTitle: Quantum Polarization in Two-Mode Generalized Binomial State
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study investigates quantum polarization in a two-mode generalized binomial state (TMGBS), a non-classical property of light, using quantum Stokes parameters and crucial in terms of its relationship to the purity and coherence of quantum states. Here we explore the criterion of quantum polarization in a generalized binomial state of light, which features a binomial photon number distribution in light pulses. Previous work by our group has examined other higher-order nonclassicality in single-and two-mode systems of GBS. Here we focus on the degree of polarization, an essential factor for observing entanglement in two-mode quantum states. Our findings emphasize the role of quantum polarization in detecting entanglement between optical modes, a fundamental resource for quantum communication protocols, including quantum teleportation and cryptography. The study demonstrates that TMGBS is an optimal candidate for achieving high degrees of quantum polarization under varied parameters, providing insights that could advance quantum technologies like quantum communication and metrology, where entanglement is pivotal.

articleTitle: Efficient Disease Diagnosis Platform: Multi-Model Solution for Early Health Condition Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-disease prediction system that leverages machine learning to enable the early diagnosis of five conditions: diabetes, heart disease, Parkinson's, breast cancer, and pneumonia. Unlike single-disease models, this system integrates diverse diagnostic tasks into a unified framework, delivering high accuracy across multiple diseases. Classification algorithms Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoostare employed to identify the optimal model for each condition, achieving up to 97.66% accuracy in breast cancer detection. For pneumonia, a 14-layer Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to analyze chest X-ray images effectively. The systems single-user interface facilitates rapid, data-driven predictions, streamlining clinical workflows and supporting proactive disease management.

articleTitle: A Sigmoid Filter Proportionate Normalized LMS Algorithm for Sparse Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Formerly, a least mean square algorithm employing a sigmoid framework (SLMS) was developed to cope with the impulsive noise. However, the SLMS technique was sparse agnostic, and the LMS approach has a gradient noise amplification issue. To address the point, the SLMS algorithm is updated to sigmoid normalized LMS (SNLMS), and to adjust for sparsity, a filter proportionate adaptation principle is applied to the SNLMS method, yielding the SFPNLMS algorithm. Finally, simulation results show that the innovative SFPNLMS technique is more resistant in an impulsive environment and has a rapid convergence for identification of the sparse systems than other current algorithms.

articleTitle: CapsNet-Based Deep Learning Approach for Robust Image Forgery Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: One common form of image tampering is image manipulation, where a section of an image is duplicated and pasted within the same image to conceal or replicate content. Detecting such manipulations is essential in digital image forensics, especially in critical domains like journalism, law enforcement, and social media. Traditional image manipulation detection methods struggle with identifying tampered regions due to sophisticated forgery techniques and post-processing like scaling, rotation, and noise addition. In this paper, we explore the application of Capsule Networks (CapsNets) in detecting copy-move or splicing image manipulation. CapsNets offer an advantage in preserving spatial hierarchies between features and improving detection performance under transformations. Experimental results demonstrate that CapsNets outperform conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in detecting copy-move or splicing forgery under various conditions, including scaling, rotation, and added noise.

articleTitle: A Review on Remote Patient Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a literature review on the role of Internet of things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) in remote patient monitoring systems (RPM). The integration of the IoT and AI into healthcare, has transformed patient care by enabling continuous, real-time health monitoring and personalized assistance. This paper discusses the general architecture of RPM and explores the recent advances in IoT and AI based RPM, focusing on their role in improving patient care outcomes, enhancing healthcare delivery, and addressing challenges such as data security, interoperability, and network reliability. Future directions in this area are suggested wherein Retrieval-Augmented Generator model (RAG) and conversational AI technologies may be incorporated into the patient monitoring system to offer accessible and responsive healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: Study and Experimental Analysis of High-Performance Low-Power ALU Using FinFET Device
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is an important component of the CPU that is used to perform arithmetical and logical operations. This paper proposes the FinFET-ALU. It can do five operations: AND, OR, addition, subtraction, and Set Less-Than (SLT) operations. It works with 18nm FinFET technology and runs on 0.6 V. There's a 4-to-1 multiplexer built using the transmission gate technique. This has an inverter at the output to help create that full swing output. For original output, inverted input is provided, the AND & OR tasks use inputs as NAND & NOR, making it perform really well. A 10-transistor (10T) full adder is used. This adder gives us an inverted carry-out, which helps with the Set Less-Than (SLT) operation. For subtraction It uses a 2-to-1 multiplexer together with the full adder. It only consumes 162.3 nW of power. The rise time is about 607.113 ps, and the fall time is just 58.893 ps. articleTitle: Analysis of Feed Network Efficiency in Time-Modulated Elliptical Antenna Array for 5G and 6G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel design strategy for a 20-element Time-Modulated Asymmetric Elliptical Antenna Array (ATMEAA) aimed at optimizing far-field radiation patterns for 5G and 6G communication systems. The design focuses on minimizing interference by reducing sidelobe levels (SLLs) and sideband levels (SBLs), both of which are critical for enhancing signal quality in high-frequency communication environments. To achieve ultra-low SLLs and SBLs, an optimal combination of switch-ON time sequences and progressive phase delays is employed. These parameters are fine-tuned using advanced metaheuristic optimization techniques, namely Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) and Sail Fish Optimization (SFO) techniques. The practical implementation of ATMEAA is analyzed at a fundamental operating frequency of 2.4 GHz. Key performance metrics such as SLLs, SBLs, feed network efficiency, and directivity are evaluated using the GWO and SFO methods. The results demonstrate significant improvements in reducing unwanted radiation components and boosting antenna performance. This approach ensures the antenna array is well-suited for high-performance applications in next-generation 5G and 6G wireless communication networks, where minimizing interference and maximizing efficiency are paramount for reliable and high-speed data transmission.

articleTitle: Challenges in Infrared Small-Target Detection: A Benchmark of YOLO Models on UAV and Bird Infrared Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Detecting small objects in infrared (IR) images, such as birds and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), presents significant challenges due to their reduced size, limited pixel representation, and lack of distinct features. These challenges are further complicated in real-world environments where complex backgrounds, such as skies, clouds, and vegetation, combined with low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and low signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), obscure the targets. Existing detection models often struggle to accurately detect small targets due to low contrast and indistinct edges. This highlights the need for detection techniques tailored to small object detection in infrared imagery. In this study, we evaluate the performance of various You Only Look Once (YOLO) models, focusing on their applicability and limitations for detecting small infrared objects. The novelty of this work lies in systematically analyzing the impact of preprocessing techniques and fine-tuning on detection performance. Fine-tuned YOLO models are evaluated for small target detection, with their strengths and weaknesses identified under diverse conditions. Insights are provided for adapting these models to enhance real-time surveillance systems in critical applications.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Shadows: DarkNET Traffic Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, with the expansion of Internet usage and web browsing, a part of the public network has emerged as the “darknet”, which is an environment for illegal activities. To identify and classify this type of network traffic, machine learning and deep learning models are used in intrusion detection systems (IDS). This paper proposes a deep learning-Bayes estimator to build a DarkNET traffic classification model, with the aim of finding the architecture of the model in traffic discrimination. The method uses the Bayes estimator algorithm to search for the optimal hyperparameter configuration of the deep learning model, thereby improving the discrimination accuracy. The deep learning Bayes estimator achieves an accuracy of 98.52% when the model is applied to the CIC-Darknet2020 dataset. Although the proposed method effectively improves the accuracy of the model, it requires longer training time during the hyperparameter finding and initial model creation stage.

articleTitle: Automated Snoring Detection System Using Synchrosqueezed Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for the recognition of snoring audio signals by applying advanced signal processing method, synchrosqueezed wavelet transform (SWT) and various machine learning classifiers such as VGG19, ResNet50, MobileNetV3, MobileNetV1, EfficientNetB7, DenseNet121, Xception, MobileNetV2, GoogleNet, and InceptionV3. Initially, the audio signals are preprocessed and further time-frequency representations (TFRs) have been obtained with the help of SWT. The obtained TFRs are then inputted into the machine learning classifiers to classifiy the snoring and non-snoring audio signals. Performance metrics in terms of accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, F1-score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) are computed. Highest accuracy of 96.5% is obtained by using the classifiers, VGG19 and ResNet50. This proposed methodology is suitable for real-time detection of snoring and can be used for diagnosis of sleep disorders such as sleep apnea.

articleTitle: First-Order Current-Mode All-Pass Frequency Selective Circuit with Single DCCII and Minimal Component Count
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, a high-output impedance, current-mode, first-order all-pass frequency-selective circuit is presented, using a single second-generation differential current conveyor (DCCII), one resistor, and one capacitor. By minimizing active and passive components, the design eliminates the requirement for element matching. Operating with a ±0.9 V power supply, the frequency selective circuit is designed using a 180 nm CMOS process. The theoretical analyses account for the effects of non-idealities and parasitic inherent in the DCCII. PSPICE simulations validate the theoretical aspects, and process, voltage, and temperature analyses confirm the effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Functional and Non-Functional Requirement (FR and NFR) Formation Based on Requirement Elicitation Using Text Semantics in IdVar4CL Artifact
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Elicitations are mandatory in establishing both Functional Requirements (FR) and Non-Functional Requirements (NFR). One of the challenges in software engineering is to ensure that Requirement Elicitation (RE) is accurately converted to well-structured FRs and NFRs in Software Requirements Specification (SRS) documentation. However, traditional approaches for requirements gathering often face challenges such as incomplete information, evolving requirements, and lack of stakeholder involvement. To address this problem, we adopted agile methodologies in software development. Hence, this study proposed to form FR and NFR based on RE through a semantic text process. The results showed that we have been successful in establishing FR and NFR on the RE process using text semantics in the IdVar4CL artifact, which included 29 documents (d1-d29), consisting of 12 RE documents, 10 FR documents and 7 NFR documents. In detail, the list of Requirement Specification tabulations in Subject, modals, Verb, Object format. Semantic similarity through comparison of the elicitation documentation with the SRS documentation results in a difference of 0.09 as a reference to subsequent SRS artifact formation improvements. Hence, this approach improves the clarity and alignment of requirements using agile development.

articleTitle: Generating Avatar Using HamNoSys and SiGML for British Sign Language
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In today's digital world online video lectures have become a crucial tool for learning. Yet, these resources aren't available to a big part of the world's population those who are deaf or hard of hearing. This study presents a new system that aims to make these resources available to everyone by turning spoken words from video lectures into sign language gestures. The system uses advanced video processing to change spoken words into text. It then turns this text into British Sign Language (BSL) glosses, which are then written in the Hamburg Notation System (HamNoSys). Using the Signing Gesture Markup Language (SiGML), the system creates a virtual avatar that can show complex sign language gestures. The heart of this research is in combining cutting-edge technologies to offer a deep learning experience that goes beyond hearing limits and tries to make online education for everyone. Early tests of the system show it has the power to close the current gap in education highlighting how important it is to include everyone in the digital age.

Author Keywords: deaf and hard of hearing community

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Security Through Double Steganography Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The growth of internet users aligns closely with population growth, with more people going online each year. As internet usage expands, both individuals and companies increasingly prioritize privacy in their digital activities, making data security a key concern. In the field of steganography, double steganography plays a significant role by offering enhanced data security through the combination of multiple embedding techniques. This study focuses on double steganography in the spatial domain, utilizing the LSB, ISB, and MSB methods. The MSB-LSB technique emerges as the optimal choice for small data sizes (10 kb), achieving SAW scores ranging from 1.073 to 1.240, PSNR values between 51.93 and 53.92 dB, and a near-perfect SSIM of 1.00. Additionally, the method demonstrates a low BER of 0.03-0.05 and an efficient processing time of approximately 1.94-1.95 seconds, ensuring excellent embedding quality with minimal distortion for small data sizes. For larger data sizes (30 kb, 50 kb, and 90 kb), the LSB-LSB and ISB-LSB approaches alternate as the most effective techniques. These methods deliver reliable embedding quality with SAW scores ranging from 0.787 to 0.954, PSNR values between 51.14 and 51.21 dB, and a consistent SSIM of 1.00. Processing times increase with data size, ranging from 2.79 to 6.38 seconds, while the BER remains stable at 0.06 for larger loads. Due to their ability to balance quality and performance, the LSB-LSB and ISB-LSB methods are better suited for embedding larger datasets.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Detection Using Bidirectional Empirical Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a progressively deteriorated, irreversible brain ailment that impairs memory and cognitive function. Early detection of Alzheimer's disease is crucial as it can reduce the risk factors and can provide the effective therapy to the affected person within stipulated time. In the proposed approach, bidirectional empirical mode decomposition is applied on 2-D Magnetic Resonance Images to decompose them into four Intrinsic Mode Functions. Then, using four Intrinsic Mode Functions, the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix has been computed. The Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix interacts directly with the image intensity, it offers information on patterns that mutually occur. For every Intrinsic Mode Functions, 22 statistical features are obtained from these matrices. In order to improve the classification accuracy, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is further utilized for extracting optimal and relevant features. The classification results for proposed method are 96.4% accuracy, 96.0 % sensitivity and 97.0 % specificity. The proposed work outperforms the existing methods for AD detection in terms of its outstanding classification results.

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis and Machine Learning Classification of Chronic Kidney Disease: Insights into Causes and Complications
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As a component of the United Nations' 2030 Agenda, Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG 3) aims to improve access to healthcare and increase global health by tackling a variety of health issues, including both infectious and non-communicable diseases. Roughly 9.5% of people worldwide suffer from chronic kidney failure(CKD) which is a serious health disease, with prevalence rates differing across regions. CKD progressively reduces kidney efficiency in filtering blood, leading to the accumulation of toxins and fluids in the body. These complications can result in severe health outcomes, such as cardiovascular disease, elevated blood pressure, stroke, and reduced life expectancy. To deepen insights into CKD, we applied exploratory data analysis to explore correlations between key variables and class-specific outcomes. Using five machine learning models, Logistic Regression demonstrated superior performance, attaining 98% accuracy, 98% precision, and 97% recall. Logistic Regression outperformed Linear Regression, K-Nearest Neighbor, Naive Bayes, and Decision Trees, according to 10-fold cross-validation used to validate these models.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for Identification and Categorization of Dermatological Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The integration of intelligent computing and machine learning (ML) has transformed various fields, leading to significant advancements in automation, data analysis, and decision-making processes. The diagnosis of diseases and access to healthcare services have long been in high demand, yet they face significant challenges. Machine learning offers a wide range of effective solutions for this purpose. While skin disorders may appear harmless, they can become serious if not treated properly. Among the most challenging issues in medical image processing is identifying skin conditions from clinical photos. Furthermore, identifying skin conditions by hand by medical professionals is subjective and time-consuming. Therefore, automatic skin disease prediction is necessary for both patients and dermatologists, which speeds up treatment planning. In this paper a comparitive study has been done on various classification algorithms and performed on various healthcare datasets and the most effective classification algorithm for the dermatological dataset has been identified. Classification algorithms have been compared on the basis of their classification accuracy. The study suggested that Logistic Model Trees (LMT) and Navie Bayes Algorithms can be used for the efficient classification of dermatology disorders.

articleTitle: Predicting Customer Churn Rate Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Customer churn prediction is essential for businesses aiming to retain their customer base in competitive markets. This study leverages machine learning to predict customer churn, employing models including Random Forest, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Using a real-world dataset, we analyze customer behavior features and apply these models to classify churn outcomes. Model performance is evaluated exclusively through confusion matrix metrics, which provide insights into true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives, thus enabling a direct assessment of each model's classification accuracy and misclassification tendencies.
