Results indicate that ensemble methods, especially Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, demonstrate strong performance in distinguishing churned from retained customers. The LSTM model, which considers sequential data, adds valuable temporal insight. This paper highlights the potential of various machine learning models for churn prediction, discussing model-specific advantages and limitations based on confusion matrix outcomes. Our findings underscore the role of machine learning in churn management and suggest potential areas for enhancing prediction accuracy through refined feature selection and deep learning approaches.

articleTitle: Corn Disease Severity Estimation using U2Net Based Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning-based approach for estimating the severity of maize plant diseases through Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Diseases like Northern Leaf Blight (NLB), Grey Leaf Spot (GLS), and Northern Leaf Spot (NLS) significantly hinder maize production, posing a risk to global food security. Traditional visual inspection methods, particularly in large-scale agriculture, often lack precision, leading to potential mismanagement and overuse of pesticides. This research explores the effectiveness of U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net based image enhancement as an image preprocessing tool and using a lightweight MobileNet CNN models in accurately detecting and categorizing the severity of maize diseases from images, offering a scalable solution for disease management. The model achieves high accuracy of 94.15 % in classification as well as 94% accuracy in severity estimation in 5 levels of disease severity on the field images of Northern Leaf Spot (NLS) in CD&S dataset, highlighting its potential for integration into automated agricultural monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Performance of Hybrid Software Defined Network (SDN) Through Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The paper is a comprehensive discussion of the optimization of Hybrid SDNs with the aid of metaheuristic algorithms. Hybrid SDNs include central and distributed control; it makes them very flexible and scalable. Yet, such environments are hard to optimize the resource allocation and traffic management. To address this, we propose a framework that leverages the power of metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithms (GAs), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to fine-tune network parameters and improve overall performance. The framework aims to optimize key performance indicators, including network throughput, latency, and resource utilization, while ensuring network stability and resilience. We show through extensive simulations and evaluations that our proposed approach can indeed achieve significant performance gains compared to traditional control mechanisms. The results show the potential of metaheuristic algorithms in optimizing hybrid SDN architectures and pave the way for more efficient and intelligent network management.

articleTitle: Transforming Healthcare with AI: Multimodal VQA Systems and LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In Multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs), Visual Question Answering in Medicine (VQA) is an essential activity that allows for clinically acceptable answers to questions concerning medical imagery. This could alleviate pressure on healthcare systems, especially in resource-limited countries. However, the medical VQA datasets available today are tiny, mostly focused on basic classification tasks, and devoid of semantic reasoning and clinical expertise. Our previous work proposed a VQA technique using three distinct relationship graphs—implicit, spatial, and semantic—based on the Medical-CXR-VQA dataset, mainly focuses on chest X-ray images that achieving 62% accuracy. By training an LLM technique, we improved label extraction accuracy to 80%. The labels were also thoroughly reviewed with two clinical specialists for greater accuracy. We then introduced a larger dataset, Medical VQA-RAD dataset (VQA-Radiology), which focuses on radiology images (including X-ray, CT scan, MRIs and Ultrasounds) that includes detailed inquiries about anomalies, locations, severity, and types. Based on this dataset, We created a novel chain-of-thought and prompt engineering bio-medical multi-modal VQA technique, refined from the Llama-3-8B model using the bespoke dataset. This approach combines curated and synthesized biological data, offering significant benefits to researchers, doctors, and biomedical professionals, by improving the comprehension and generation of content related to a wide range of biological topics.

articleTitle: 5G Network Slicing Prediction Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence(X-AI)
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The emergence of 5G technology has transformed network architecture, with network slicing technology standing out as a crucial feature for managing diverse and demanding applications. This innovative technology allows the creation of multiple virtual networks within a single physical infrastructure, each dedicated to specific needs such as latency, bandwidth, and reliability. These capabilities are vital for supporting services like enhanced mobile broadband, ultra-reliable low-latency communications, and massive machine-type communications. Predicting the optimal configuration of network slices is challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of 5G environments. While traditional methods often lack the necessary accuracy, machine learning models have shown promise in addressing this challenge. However, the adoption of these models introduces the challenge of interpretability, as understanding how they reach their predictions is often difficult. In this work, we have proposed that Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques such as Permutation Feature Importance and Partial Dependency Plots could be employed to enhance the transparency of prediction of ML models. These methods provide insights into the decision-making processes of ML models, making their predictions more interpretable and trustworthy for critical 5G network management tasks.

articleTitle: Real Time Machinery Health Detection Via Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Marine vessels are equipped with advanced and integrated complex machines that operate in challenging conditions, where the failure rate is high. One of the most vital elements of these machines is fault diagnosis and maintaining 100 percent operational states. Any machinery breakdown at sea during maritime operations can have severe consequences leading to operational impacts and reducing combat efficiency. The existing maintenance routines - PPM (Planned Preventive Maintenance) and CBPM (Condition Based Predictive Maintenance) are reactive approaches that may miss early signs of material degradation, leading to unplanned machinery breakdown at sea. An efficient method to counter this issue in real time is thermal imaging. The dataset required to develop a thermal prognostic model for real-time machinery health detection is not available. This paper presents a systematic approach to develop a prognostic model for real time machinery health detection via thermal imaging. We have developed a custom thermal image dataset representing various machinery conditions-normal, defective and degraded. We have developed our real-time prognostic model ‘Thermal Prognostic Model’. This model targets fuel systems to prevent major fires and accidents at sea by predicting potential failures and taking corrective actions with mAP50 0.956, precision 0.945 and recall 0.957.

articleTitle: Smart Gym Assistant: Posture Monitoring and Rep Counting
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Many workout applications offer their users a set of videos to follow, where users have no opportunity to have their form corrected in real time. This approach can lead to unnatural alignment, increase the risk of injury and diminish the usefulness of the exercises. The workout pose corrector with an attached integrated repetition counter is the focus of this paper for improving performance and reducing the possibility of injury while exercising. The system employs state-of-the-art computer vision technology and machine learning algorithms to record video and analyze real-time body position during exercises. It provides error feedback information to the user from the evaluation of skeletal points against that of the ideal pose of a specific exercise. It also contains a counter mechanism which is activated only when the exercise is performed correctly. The information from the experiments revealed that the pose detection system was trained and tested with a precision of 98. 3% during training and 96. 4% during testing, while guaranteeing that the users perform the necessary exercises in the right form.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Predicting Molecular Refractivity in Drug Toxicology
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The integration of electronics engineering into molecular refractivity prediction is transforming drug toxicology studies. By combining biosensors, machine learning algorithms, and high-speed data systems, scientists can better predict toxicological profiles of drugs. This interdisciplinary approach improves safety and efficacy in drug development. Electronics engineering enables real-time monitoring of drug metabolism through wearable devices and predictive models, identifying toxic metabolites early and reducing adverse reactions. These technologies enhance the assessment of metabolic processes, guiding safer drug development. Machine learning algorithms further refine predictions by analyzing large datasets, identifying toxicity patterns, and improving personalized treatment plans, ultimately reducing time and costs in toxicology testing. In this research work, machine learning classifier accuracy has been achieved 85% to identify toxic drugs and toxicity prediction accuracy by using the Bayesian Neural Network was 95.8%.

articleTitle: Cutting Edge Weapon Detection in Real-Time CCTV Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In today's world, ensuring public safety through advanced surveillance systems is critical. This paper presents a cutting-edge weapon detection system that operates in real-time using CCTV video streams, leveraging deep learning algorithms such as YOLO (You Only Look Once) and Detectron2. The system is designed to detect and classify weapons, such as guns and knives, with high accuracy while maintaining low latency. Through the use of optimized deep learning models, the system processes live video feeds and identifies potential threats in real-time, providing immediate alerts to security personnel. The proposed system is scalable, supporting multiple video feeds. The paper explores the methodologies employed to achieve real-time processing, including frame extraction, model inference, and post-processing techniques like Non-Maximum Suppression. Optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, and hardware acceleration are applied to ensure the system runs efficiently on edge devices. Extensive testing was conducted in real-world environments, demonstrating the system's ability to handle diverse lighting conditions, occlusions, and varying weapon types. The results show significant improvements in detection accuracy, response time, and system reliability, making it a valuable addition to modern security solutions. Furthermore, the system adheres to privacy laws, ensuring compliance in surveillance applications. This paper contributes to the advancement of automated surveillance systems by providing an efficient and effective solution for weapon detection in public and private spaces.

articleTitle: Honeypot-Based Security System for Intrusion Detection and User Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The world is becoming increasingly digital day by day, and cyberattacks are rising in both volume and complexity, imposing huge threats to the personal and organizational domains. Firewalls and antivirus programs, which had been developed to provide security for individuals and organizations, fail to effectively respond to new intrusion tactics. The honeypot-based security system designed in this paper detects and reacts to unauthorized accesses in a stealthy manner. The system identifies correct and incorrect login credentials and provides access to legitimate users while sending suspected intruders to a decoy site, which creates the impression that the login attempt has been successful. This setup captures valuable intruder data such as IP address, geolocation, attempted passwords, and webcam captured images without alerting the intruder. The system automatically sends an alert email to the registered user, with key details like location data and the intruder's photo if an intrusion is detected after multiple failed login attempts. It was tested to log unauthorized activities reliably and issue the necessary notifications on time, which makes it practical and effective in detecting suspicious access. This approach shows how honey pots can be integrated into proactive, cyber-enhancement strategies, providing an insight and advancement for future intrusion detection strategies.

articleTitle: Multi-Hop Satellite Communications Link Analysis in the South Pacific Region
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Multi-hop satellite communication has a very important role to play in enhancing the existing communication network in far and wide-flung regions like Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Vanuatu, and other South Pacific Island nations where such islands are dispersed, which makes it difficult to set up better communications systems. The analysis of the multi-hop satellite communication link is performed with MATLAB for this project and addresses such problems of the South Pacific countries as having a ground station in Port Vila, Vanuatu, and the other in IIT Delhi, India, with such extensive ocean coverage and with many sparsely inhabited islands. Signal propagation models, link budgeting estimation, and multiple hop relay are used in this process, while the performance evaluation is done in terms of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), bit error rate (BER), and bandwidth usage efficiency. Through this work, using the powerful MATLAB simulation tools, it is possible to get important findings on how to balance the number of satellite middle hops required for reliable communication with the minimal possible latency and maximum coverage area. The current findings suggest that the multi-hop setup greatly increases link reliability and reduces the need for high-power transmitters, making the enhancement of communication infrastructure in the South Pacific more cost-effective. Thus, this work imposes current and aspiring improvements toward applying the satellite communication systems applicable to rural and remote areas in the given region.

articleTitle: Predicting Stock Market Movements in Response to Global Events
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Stock market has been using prediction models that have often focused on historical data, giving less attention to how external factors like elections, inflation and conflicts affect the stock prices. This proposal examines the influence possessed by these external factors on stock market behaviour. Machine learning models, including Random Forest, Linear Regression, Gradient Boosting and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), is applied as well as investigated on the live dataset of Yahoo Finance, Geopolitical Data, Covid-19 Data and Inflation in GDP, to see which algorithm performs best in predicting the changes in stock value caused by the external factors. The best-case accuracy was 99.9%, showing the importance of consideration of external events for more accurate stock market predictions in the real world. This will help investors make better decisions and improve the risk management strategies required in business.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Real-Time Exercise Repetition Counting System
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Real-time exercise detection is a challenging problem. Hence, we present a real-time exercise detection system that addresses the challenge of accurately monitoring exercises without the need for an expensive, real-life coach. Our approach leverages machine learning techniques to detect errors in exercises and provide actionable feedback, making fitness training more accessible and affordable. First, we collect a dataset, capturing multiple video frames with joint landmarks represented as key points in each image. These images are labeled with exercise actions such as curls, presses, and squats. Then, we perform data cleaning and splitting. After that we have trained and evaluated two machine learning models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Random Forest based on metrics, namely, accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score. From our experimental results, we have found that the LSTM model outperforms the Random Forest, demonstrating its superior effectiveness in real-time exercise detection. Our results highlight the potential of AI-driven systems to provide personalized fitness guidance, opening doors to innovative solutions in the health and fitness industry.

articleTitle: Beyond Limits: Machine Learning Driven Reliability Forecasting for Nanoscale ULSI Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning-based predictive model for negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) degradation in nanoscale PMOS transistors. Through extensive HSPICE Synopsys simulations over a decade, encompassing diverse process and bias conditions, the study elucidates the influence of Gate Oxide, Threshold Voltage, Temperature, and Supply Voltage on NBTI. Multiple machine learning algorithms including Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, Tree Regression, Ensembles of Trees Regression, Gaussian Process Regression, and Neural Networks are trained and validated. Results showcase more than 99% accuracy in forecasting NBTI degradation, facilitating robust design strategies for VLSI digital circuits in industrial 45nm technology nodes.

articleTitle: Evaluating Machine Learning Algorithms for Effective Credit Card Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study studies Machine Learning (ML) algorithms for tracing credit card fraud, including random forest, logistic regression, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), using a dataset of 287,807 transactions from European cardholders. To resolve data imbalance, resampling was done after applying data preparation techniques. Ten balanced subsets of data were produced by undersampling the majority (non-fraud) class, each of which concentrated on a different aspect of the majority. These subsets were used to train individual models, and predictions were produced by majority voting. For comparison, models were trained using the original unbalanced data in addition to resampling. Accuracy, recall, precision, F1 scores, ROC-AVC scores, and a practical business assessment to determine their practical relevance were among the evaluation criteria. Logistic regression, trained on unbalanced data, achieved a ROC-AUC of 99.06% with transparent decision-making, outperforming models trained on balanced subsets, which, despite high AUC-ROC scores, suffered low precision and reduced practical reliability in fraud detection.

articleTitle: Exploring Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Enhanced Accuracy in Medical Imaging and Early Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods in medical imaging has completely changed how early disease screening is done, leading to big gains in accuracy, speed, and patient results. This essay looks at how AI can improve medical images. It focuses on deep learning algorithms, computer vision, and machine learning models that can make complicated diagnosis tasks easier to do automatically. These technologies make it possible to find and study small trends in medical pictures that a person might miss. This helps doctors make faster and more accurate diagnoses, especially in cancer, heart, and neurology. AI can find problems in X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and its performance is on par with or even better than that of expert doctors. The paper also looks at how AI can be used to predict diseases by looking at old image data along with clinical factors. Researchers are looking at techniques like reinforcement learning and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to see if they can improve picture quality and help make fake data for rare diseases. This will help make diagnosis tools that are more accurate. The study also shows how AI is becoming more and more important for solving problems like inconsistent data, picture noise, and wrong interpretations. As healthcare continues to go digital, adding AI to medical imaging systems could help with personalized treatment plans, lower the number of mistakes made during diagnosis, and speed up work processes.

articleTitle: Advancing Grammatical Error Correction for English Text: A Comparative Study of Bahdanau Attention and Multi-Head Attention Models
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: English Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) is a vital aspect of Natural Language Processing (NLP), aimed at enhancing text accuracy and readability by resolving grammatical errors. This study examines the performance of two models: the Multi-Head Attention-Based Seq2Seq model and the Bahdanau Attention model, tested on multiple datasets. While the Multi-Head Attention model achieves strong results, the Bahdanau Attention model outperforms it, achieving a higher accuracy of 99.72%. The Bahdanau model's ability to capture contextual nuances more effectively contributes to its superior performance in correcting grammatical mistakes. These findings position the Bahdanau model as a state-of-the-art approach in GEC, demonstrating its advanced capability to handle complex linguistic structures. The research underscores the potential for the refinement of grammatical correction techniques through innovative model architectures.

articleTitle: Automated Power Quality Assessment Using IEVDHM Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a new framework for the classification of power quality (PQ) disturbances based on improved eigenvalue decomposition of Hankel matrix (IEVDHM) and Hilbert transform separation algorithm (HTSA). IEVDHM decomposes a disturbance signal into a set of mono-component signals. Further, HTSA technique computes the amplitude envelope (AE), instantaneous phase (IP), and instantaneous frequency of the decomposed mono-component signals. The 5 time-dependent spectral features (TDSFs) and 6 HTSA-based features are extracted from each decomposed mono-component signals. The TDSFs are logarithmic zero order spectral moment, logarithmic difference of zero order and second order spectral moment, logarithmic difference of zero order and fourth order spectral moment, spectral sparseness and irregularity factor. Whereas, the HTSA-based features are mean of AE, energy of mono-component signal, standard deviation of AE, standard deviation of IP, envelope entropy, and mean frequency. Then, the bagged decision tree, optimizable neural network, and linear support vector machine classify these extracted features into 19 different types of disturbance classes. The bagged decision tree-based classifier has achieved an accuracy of 92.48 %, 91.07 %, 88.98 %, 88.01 % for clean PQ signals, noisy (additive white Gaussian noise) PQ signals with signal to noise ratios 60 dB, 40 dB, and 20 dB, respectively. The performance of the proposed framework is compared with the performance of empirical mode decomposition (EMD), ensemble EMD, and variational mode decomposition-based frameworks for PQ detection and is found to be superior.

Author Keywords: improved eigenvalue decomposition of Hankel matrix

articleTitle: Enhancing Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access with Practical Successive Interference Cancellation: A MIMO Approach with Interference-Predicted MMSE Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the realm of forthcoming wireless mobile networks, non-orthogonal multiple access, commonly referred to as NOMA, has been identified as a viable radio access technique. It employs successive interference cancellation (SIC) as the primary receiver mechanism and utilizes the power domain for user multiplexing on the transmitter side, anticipating advancements in mobile devices. Nonetheless, a substantial segment of the latest research endeavors to evaluate the effectiveness of NOMA on the assumption that the receiver has full SIC capability. This study examines the potential to reconcile the disparity between the theoretical and actual efficacy of successive interference cancellation (SIC) in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems by employing multi-input multi-output (MIMO) technology with zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) SIC methodologies. This document presents the interference-predicted minimum mean square error (IPMMSE) interference cancellation (IC) method, which modifies the MMSE weight factor to accommodate interference signals. Furthermore, they provide a study of the error consequences linked to practical SIC designs. We propose the remaining interference-predicted MMSE (RIPMMSE) interference cancellation as a resolution to the issue of residual interference, based on this premise. On the other hand, the findings of the simulation show that the suggested IC schemes that forecast interference signals outperform NOMA with standard ZF and MMSE IC techniques. This is despite the fact that practical IC schemes produce a higher bit error rate (BER) in comparison to traditional orthogonal multiple access (OMA).

articleTitle: Vidhya: A Virtual Tutor for Enhancing English Education in Rural Areas of India
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the new age of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalisation, English proficiency is a very significant need for any individual to strive in this digital world. In this work, the authors focus on developing an online virtual English tutor bot called “Vidhya”. This platform aims to provide an accessible and interactive English learning platform for students aged 13 to 18 from rural areas of India. The platform is designed to improve the speaking and writing skills of learners at their own pace of learning. The platform is designed in several levels which give the user a similar experience to playing a game with levels. This is introduced to make the user feel achievement and motivation to use the system. The system gives students the freedom to make mistakes and repeat the process until they learn and gain a retention threshold to move to the next level. The software platform is intended to support the rural Indian student community in learning English and propel them to pursue their academic and employment opportunities. The design features an intelligent feedback system wherein the software listens to the learners and provides feedback to them pointing out where they have to improve.

articleTitle: Generative AI Meets IoT: A Bibliometric Mapping of Research and Development
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Computer technology has transformed the way people interact online within society. The integration of (GIoT) combines Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology, offering numerous benefits in many fields for innovation and growth. GIoT helps with real-time applications for data prediction and alerts. Based on the authors' understanding and searches in scholarly databases, less bibliometric analysis has yet been performed on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) for the IoT, even though such analyses are crucial for research development in this field. This study conducted a thorough bibliometric examination of GAI applications in the IoT over the period from 2014 to 2024. The analysis is based on a dataset of 296 documents sourced from the Scopus database. The bibliometric review was conducted using the Biblioshiny application, a tool available within the Bibliometric package in the R programming language. Top literature sources, major fields of study, nations, well-known authors, popular subjects, authorship, citations, author-keywords, and co-keywords were all subjected to bibliometric analysis.

articleTitle: Advanced Sleep Stage Classification Through a Convolutional Recurrent Attention-Based Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Sleep stage classification plays a critical role in diagnosing sleep disorders, which are linked to cognitive and physical health issues. Polysomnography (PSG) is commonly used for this purpose, but manual classification is time-consuming and prone to error. This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning model combining Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks with attention mechanisms to classify PSG signals from single electroencephalogram (EEG) channels into five sleep stages. The model captures both spatial and temporal features from the EEG data, addressing class imbalance through random under-sampling. Experimental results on the Sleep-EDF dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, with promising accuracy and F1-score metrics, outperforming traditional methods and offering improved classification robustness.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Detecting Anomaly in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) presents a novel method for collaborative model training while safeguarding data privacy, which is a primary concern in the Internet of Things (IoT) world. This research uses FL to enhance security within IoT networks, employing the CICIoT2023 dataset. The dataset was subjected to important preprocessing, including the management of missing data and the removal of redundancies, with feature selection conducted using a Random Forest classifier to determine essential attributes. These features were incorporated into a simulated FL framework, where locally trained models from decentralized datasets contributed to a collectively aggregated model. Our findings reveal the capacity of FL to improve model accuracy without sacrificing data privacy, offering scalable and practical security solutions for IoT systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive CEEMD-SVD Joint Denoising Algorithm via Aquila Optimization in FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Noise contamination in frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar signals significantly impairs target detection and results in inaccurate range and velocity measurements. To tackle this issue, an adaptive CEEMD - SVD joint denoising algorithm is put forward in this paper. By utilizing the aquila optimizer (AO) for noise reduction for the intermediate frequency (IF) signal of the FMCW radar, we get what is called as the AO-CEEMD-SVD denoising algorithm. Firstly, the original IF signal of the FMCW radar is decompose into a series of intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). Secondly, the Person correlation coefficient (PCC) method is utilized to identify IMFs demonstrating a significant relationship with the original signal. Thirdly, these selected IMFs are subjected to singular value decomposition (SVD), preserving a suitable count of the most significant singular values. The denoised signal is then reconstructed by integrating the processed IMFs with the residual components. Subsequently, the AO algorithm is utilized to construct a fitness function and search for the optimal parameter set for signal denoising. Finally, the optimal parameter set is used to perform CEEMD-SVD-based denoising and signal reconstruction to obtain the final denoised signal. Simulation experiments are conducted to validate the efficacy of the proposed AO-CEEMD-SVD denoising method, benchmarking it against current denoising techniques. The results indicate that the AO-CEEMD-SVD approach exhibits superior noise suppression performance and surpasses existing methods. Moreover, it achieves enhanced denoising performance for the FMCW radar signals.

articleTitle: Functional Connectivity and Power Spectral Density Analysis of EEG Signals in Meditation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Meditation, an old practice of many traditions, has been getting a lot of attention for its supposed ability to relax and relieve stress. However, the neurophysiological mechanisms behind these effects are relatively unexplored. In this survey paper we look at the current literature of EEG based analytical methodologies (Functional Connectivity, Power Spectral Density/PSD) to study the effects of meditation on cerebral activity and evaluate the trustworthiness of these studies. We describe a global view of the brain wave patterns associated with relaxation and cognitive functions, that we can characterize precisely in terms of mediated with meditation. The paper also presents the implementation of the Functional Connectivity metrics like, weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI), and their evaluations to characterize the brain network coupling during meditative states. We then evaluate PSD analysis as a way to evaluate variations of brain wave power distribution during meditation. Despite the widespread availability of these technologies, current research is missing substantial detail, especially regarding the empirical application of sophisticated EEG methods to demonstrate the therapeutic effect of meditation as demonstrated with this survey. Although meditation has been found to have multiple benefits, little has been studied about the neurophysiology responsible for it. The purpose of this work is to propose an integrated framework for future research that integrates diverse methodologies to elucidate the scientific basis of meditation's effects. Yet the implications of such research could be profound in the arena of clinical practice, yet existing findings do not seem to be sufficiently rigorous. In addition, this discussion also addresses index terms such as meditation, EEG Analysis, Functional Connectivity, Power Spectral Density (PSD) and Neurophysiological Effects so that a clearer idea of the intricate connection between these diverse aspects can be had.

articleTitle: Regional Analysis of Influential Meteorological Factors in Daily Precipitation Forecasting Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Severe precipitation conditions create a substantial risk to lives of individuals. For the management of reservoirs, food production and city development, accurate daily precipitation prediction is essential. This study explores the utilization of different Machine Learning (ML) models for forecasting precipitation based on 21 years of meteorological data from Narela, Rohini, Anand Vihar and Okhla of Delhi, India. The dataset contains meteorological features such as WS2M (wind speed at 2 meters), T2M (temperature at 2 meters), T2MDEW (dew point temperature at 2 meters), T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M (relative humidity at 2 meters), PS (surface pressure), WS10M (wind speeds at 10m), WS10M_MIN, WS10M_MAX and precipitation, with precipitation as the target variable. The performance of several Machine Learning (ML) models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and hybrid model of Convolutional Neural Network and Long Short Term Memory (CNN-LSTM), is compared. Out of all of these models, the CNN-LSTM model performs the best, showing the lowest RMSE and highest R2 across all 4 locations. The results demonstrate the ability of Machine Learning (ML) models, particularly CNN-LSTM, to significantly enhance the precision of precipitation predictions. These findings emphasize the potential of hybrid Machine Learning (ML) models in providing accurate daily precipitation forecasts, especially in urban areas with complex weather patterns and hence underscore the significance of advanced Machine Learning (ML) methods in improving the accuracy of precipitation forecasts, which are vital for applications such as water resource management and hydrological modelling in urban areas like Delhi. The current research relies on the ability to alter city climatology and planning, enhance making decisions using accurate precipitation predictions, and help to mitigate the effects of disasters.

Author Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network and Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM)

articleTitle: Barley Root and Shoot Growth Dynamics in Deep Water Culture Hydroponics: Comparative Analysis Using AquaCrop Simulator
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Catering to the prevailing agricultural issues like depleted arable land, climatic uncertainty, food security, higher demands of medicinal plants, etc. is a dire requirement of the urban society. Medicinal plants serve the multiple purposes of ensuring the good health of the natives and improving the economy of any nation. The growth responses of agricultural production greatly depend upon various factors like substrate for cultivation, energy consumption, resource availability and utilization, space utilization, and pests and disease management. This study conducts a comparative analysis of two separate forms of vertical farming: hydroponic and soil cultivation, by examining the growth responses of a herbaceous medicinal plant - barley. The yield comparison in both mediums is done to analyze and identify the best-suited cultivation method and the obtained growth responses are simulated in the ‘AquaCrop’ simulator to validate the actual results. The methodology of this study is a valuable tool to enhance sustainable agriculture and solve global agriculture problems. This study also enhances sustainable agriculture by showing how hydroponic cultivation works and fulfilling many other sustainable development goals like ‘no poverty’, ‘zero hunger’, ‘good health and well-being’, ‘industry innovation and infrastructure’, and ‘responsible production and consumption’.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Facial Emotion Recognition: Insights from EmoNet
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Facial emotion classification is critical in improving human-computer interaction and applications like affective computing and mental health monitoring. Accurate recognition of emotions from images enables systems to better understand and respond to human emotional states. However, existing algorithms face challenges in capturing subtle emotional expressions, handling variations in facial features due to lighting, angles, or occlusion, and generalizing effectively across diverse datasets. EmoNet addresses these challenges through its CNN-based architecture, designed specifically for emotion classification from facial images. It utilizes convolutional layers to extract spatial features, followed by fully connected layers for classifying emotions. EmoNet excels in processing complex facial expressions, adapting to different lighting and occlusion conditions, and generalizing across varied datasets. This makes it highly suitable for real-time applications requiring accurate emotion recognition. The performance of EmoN et is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which highlight its effectiveness in handling diverse real-world scenarios. Notably, EmoN et achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.6% and a Kappa score of 94.1, establishing it as the top performer across all emotional categories.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Biomarker Discovery and Risk Prediction in Autoimmune Disease Genetics
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Autoimmune diseases are diseases where the body immune system targets on the body tissues. These conditions are polygenic in that they implicate multiple genes and gene by context interactions. Evaluating the human genomes is a complicated process because it is high dimensionality and epistatic interactions between many genes. Standard biochemical-genetic approaches can fail to provide the answers to these questions, so using supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms has been shown to help in understanding such diseases. Thus, using techniques of ML for processing big genomic data can reveal significant patterns. This work employs the XGBoost classifier to demonstrate examples of applying ML in the field of autoimmune diseases diagnostics based on genetic data. Therefore, we used the feature selection technique, data imputation, clinical and genetic feature engineering, and hyperparameters optimization. The optimizer reaches 94.75% accuracy concluding that others are compatible with inherent genes influencing autoimmune disease risk, such as WBC count. On the basis of feature importance analysis and confusion matrices, I got an idea about the distributive pattern, reasons, and pathways of these diseases. As such, these studies show the promise of ML in the biomarker discovery for screening and in the unraveling of the genetics of autoimmune diseases. As such, the approach provides future directions for the development of psychological therapies individually targeted with genetic vulnerabilities in autoimmune disease management.

articleTitle: An Efficient Automatic Car Parking Slot Allocation System
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work presents an automated car parking allocation system designed to optimize and enhance the efficiency of parking management in urban environments. The system utilizes an Arduino board and a camera to detect vehicle number plates, store pertinent information, and allocate available parking spaces effectively. By employing image processing techniques and optical character recognition (OCR), the system processes images captured by the camera to extract and display number plate data. The traditional parking systems have common challenges, such as wrong allocation of parking slots, which leads to congestion and inconvenience to users. The proposed innovative automated car parking allocation system aims to resolve common challenges in traditional parking systems by providing a more organized and automated approach. This system has been tested in various scenarios, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve operational efficiency and user satisfaction in real-time applications.

articleTitle: Use of AI/ML-Based Systems in Healthcare Domain in Reference with COVID-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Advanced technologies and day-to-day research have led to restructure of society in almost every domain, along with healthcare as well as medical sector, in respect to the last decade. Artificial intelligence (AI)/ Machine learning (ML) algorithms and technologies are being used to redesign and optimize wireless networks efficiently in prospects like measurement, estimation, and modeling of channels; research in the physical layer, etc. Multiple AI-based tools majorly assist the healthcare sector all over the globe. Automation of systems and devices has been established across the globe with the expansion of digitalisation. Automation offers and allows us to deal with the real- world problems smartly. Deep learning (DL) and AI-based systems and software allow precise analysis of the infection and counterbalance the shortage of time, resources, and staff required for imaging and diagnosis procedures. The current review is based on the application of Artificial intelligence as a principal idea in reference with the early disease detection and diagnosis with accuracy, timely treatment with precision, and moreover focuses on the prevention of various diseases through smart devices.

articleTitle: Pneumonia and Tuberculosis Classification from Chest X-ray Images Through Composite Features and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper proposed a simple and effective lung diseases classification model from CXR images through machine learning (ML) algorithms. Unlike the existing methods which used complex deep learning algorithms, this model is very simple and focused on ensuring maximum discrimination through handcrafted features. Four different set of features are used to describe CXR image in four different orientations like texture, geometry, intensity and high frequencies. At classification, an ensemble learning strategy is proposed which comprised of two ML algorithm namely Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Extreme learning Machine (ELM). SVM differentiates the input CXR images into two classes namely normal and diseased. Next, ELM differentiates the diseases image into two classes namely Pneumonia and Tuberculosis. Additionally, preprocessing is applied to improve the CXR image quality in terms of contrast enhancement and noise removal. Further, to reduce the complexity, this work processed only a Region of Interest for feature extraction followed by classification. Towards ROI extraction, a dynamic threshold mechanism is applied which drives the threshold purely based on image morphological characteristics. Extensive experiments are carried out over the proposed model with varying simulation scenarios and the obtained results prove that the proposed model is superior to the state-of-the-art methods. It aims to emphasize the significance of early detection in lung diseases, the limitations of current methods, and the suggested alternatives. The average accuracy gained by proposed model is observed as 98% which is larger than all the existing approach.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study of Loss Functions for Aspect Category Detection in Imbalanced Data Scenario
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: One of the key challenges in the Aspect Category Detection task is dealing with class imbalance in the data, which can significantly affect the performance of machine learning models. In this study, different loss functions have been analyzed to tackle the problem of class imbalance for Aspect Category Detection from textual data. A comprehensive comparative analysis of loss functions, including Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE), Weighted Binary Cross-Entropy (WBCE), Class-Balanced Cross-Entropy (CBCE), and Focal Loss have been conducted, across Bi-LSTM and Bi-GRU architectures. The performance of the models has been evaluated on two imbalanced datasets using key metrics such as precision, recall, macro <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> 1-score, accuracy and MCC. The results indicate that focal loss consistently outperforms other loss functions, particularly when used with the Bi-LSTM model, achieving the highest scores and demonstrating superior handling of class imbalance issue.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Efficient CNN Hardware of Digital Number Recognition for Low-Power
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper offers a unique convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized for digital number recognition, emphasising low powerconsumption. The project attempts to create an efficientCNN-based system capable of detecting digital numbers in power-constrained conditions. We use a cutting-edge YOLO-NAS model and FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) technology to improve processing efficiency and minimize energy consumption. The technique consists of many critical components. First, we train the YOLO-NAS model using a large dataset from Roboflow, which includes extensive annotations for digital number recognition. The model is then modified for FPGA implementation, necessitating changes to accommodate FPGA-specific limitations and assure compatibility. To enhance the model performance, we use quantization techniques and pruning strategies, particularly the L1 norm-based pruning strategy, which reduces model size and Computing demand while maintaining accuracy. Thefindings reveal that our FPGA-based YOLO-NAS modeloutperforms traditional GPU-based systems in terms of power efficiency while not influencingrecognition performance. The model performs well in real-time digital number recognition tests, showing its usefulness in low-power applications. This study overcomes the issues of power consumption and processing efficiency, providing a scalable approach appropriate for edge computing applications. By combining YOLO-NAS with FPGA, the research opens the path for more sustainable and efficient digital recognition systems.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of K-SVD, Discriminative K-SVD, and Approximate K-SVD Dictionary Learning Algorithms for Public Road Type Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In today's world, having the ability to drive has become of significant importance, especially while traveling. As a consequence, the importance of studying road safety is rising. Hence, the importance of research in designing intelligent systems to aid drivers in providing comfort, security, and safety is also gaining much momentum in recent times. On the other hand, designing Dictionary learning (DL) algorithms in conjunction with sparse representation/coding has become a forerunner in machine learning based research problems in the current decade. Many such DL based sparse solutions have been effectively proposed for a variety of signal processing and image processing algorithms. In some of our earlier works, we have shown how various dictionary learning based algorithms and system solutions can be successfully developed for home automation and ambient assisted leaving problems. Taking our research efforts in DL algorithms further, in this work we show how DL algorithms can be effectively used to categorize four common road types: urban roads, highways, residential areas, and rural areas. The algorithms have been developed based on sensory signals acquired by a driver wearing smart glasses, while driving in those road conditions. The DL based system developed can help providing guidance to a driver during driving. Three prominent varieties of DL algorithms, called K-singular value decomposition (K-SVD) algorithm, approximate K-SVD algorithm, and discriminative K-SVD algorithm, have been successfully implemented here for a benchmark, open dataset available for this problem and their suitable effectiveness has been investigated in detail. Although all the three varieties of K-SVD algorithms showed encouraging performances under different recognition problems, the discriminative K-SVD algorithm, employing orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm at its core for sparse coding purposes, emerged as the best overall performer.

articleTitle: Evaluating Machine Learning Algorithms with Feature Selection for Cybersecurity: A Case Study on Pegasus Spyware
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The growing incidence of mobile spyware attacks presents serious threats to user privacy and data security in today's digital environment. It is crucial to identify such spyware, especially complex varieties like Pegasus, in order to safeguard private and corporate data. The goal of this work is to improve spyware detection by using and contrasting three machine learning methods to detect malware activity across several datasets: Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). A considerable amount of research identifies the difficulties in this field, such as poor accuracy, excessive false positives, and a lack of multi-model comparisons that make it difficult to reliably identify spyware in many data contexts. To address this, study provides a novel approach that compares these models using dataset of Pegasus spyware. This method uses feature selection and Cross-Validation for improved performance and interpretability, is among the first to offer a reliable multi-model reference for malware detection. According to the results, the RF model has the best detection ability in all circumstances, achieving the highest accuracy of 97.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on Dataset 1, 85.6% on Dataset2, and 89.75% on Dataset3. Additionally effective are KNN and LR, which achieve accuracies of up to 89.39% and 89.72%, respectively. Our results show that RF has the potential to be a strong, dependable spyware detection solution, surpassing the 90% accuracy of previous models and establishing a new standard for future study and use in mobile security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Detection by Leveraging Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: With concerning incidence rates, lung cancer continues to be a worldwide health emergency that necessitates efficient detection techniques to enhance patient outcomes. In order to stop the progression of the disease, lower mortality, and raise survival rates, early and precise diagnosis is essential. However, because of the non-intuitive correlation between characteristics like lymph node involvement and cancer diagnosis, it can be difficult to detect cancer in its early stages, even for skilled medical professionals. To overcome these obstacles, this work uses machine learning approaches. For the categorization of lung cancer, it uses algorithms such as Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Decision Tree. These algorithms use a variety of features to analyzedata and detect the presence of cancer; preprocessing techniques like data slicing and feature scaling are applied. Performance matrices like accuracy, precision, recall and f1 score were taken into consideration. Support Vector machine outperformed other models by achieving an accuracy of 94% along with precision of 92% and recall being 97%. The outcomes highlight SVM's effectiveness in offering trustworthy diagnostic information. In order to effectively tackle this deadly disease, our study not only exhibits the promise of machine learning in early cancer diagnosis and also lays the groundwork for incorporating such approaches into clinical workflows.

articleTitle: Advancements in Automated Segmentation Techniques for Endometrial Cancer: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecological cancer that requires an accurate detection and diagnosis for effective treatment. Automated segmentation of medical images, MRI(Magnetic Resonance Imaging), PET (Positron Emission Tomography), and CT (Computed Tomography) scans, raises diagnostic accuracy, reduces human error, and assures consistent identification of tumor margins, hence, it provides early detection and personalized treatment strategies. The study focuses on several automated segmentation techniques, with particular attention on the effectiveness of U-Net Architecture for MRI images with the achievement of high Dice coefficients (0.959 for uterus and 0.911 for tumor segmentation).PET/CT images, on the other side, showed the highest Dice ever recorded was 0.739 with the PET images and 0.510 with the CT images, substantiating the difficulties of segmentation in multi-modality datasets. The low performance of automated Segmentation in PET and CT Scans, as reported in the literature, led us to review various hybrid cnn-transformer models that have demonstrated effectiveness in other tumor segmentation tasks. This study delves into the potential of imaging PET and CT and introduces promising future directions to enhance performance metrics of automated segmentation of PET and CT images.

articleTitle: Detecting Alzheimer's Disease (Gender-Based) Using Different Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the current scenario, Alzheimer's Disease constitutes 60-70% of neurodegenerative issues and affects 55 million people across the globe. As this disease progresses, the symptoms become worse and almost unmanageable. Thus, the early diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease during the onset of mild symptoms, would be highly beneficial in tackling the challenges posed by this disease. Therefore, the work performs a comparative analysis (gender-based) of various methods including Support Vector Machine, k-Nearest Neighbours, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Trees, Naïve Bayes, and Modified k-Nearest Neighbours to diagnose Alzheimer's disease. For this, the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) dataset is used. The experimental analysis revealed that the Modified k-Nearest Neighbours is 99.12%, 99.49%, and 90.32% accurate in identifying Alzheimer's irrespective of gender, in male-gender, and female-gender subjects respectively. Additionally, other renowned classifiers such as Random Forest and cubic degree polynomial kernel Support Vector Machine are 98.96% accurate in detecting Alzheimer's irrespective of gender. The same classifiers are 97.62% accurate in diagnosing male Alzheimer's patients. Likewise, for distinguishing female Demented subjects from Non-demented cohorts, Random Forest and conventional k-Nearest Neighbours (at k=5) are 88.71% accurate. With such results emphasizing gender parameters, modified k-Nearest Neighbours is found more effective in diagnosing Alzheimer's Disease than other renowned classifiers.

articleTitle: Reliability-Aware Machine Learning Prediction for Multi-Cycle Long-Term PMOS NBTI Degradation in Robust Nanometer ULSI Digital Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework to enhance the reliability of nanometer Ultra Large Scale Integrated (ULSI) digital circuits by employing advanced machine learning models to predict multi-cycle, long-term PMOS Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) degradation. The study utilizes the 32nm technology node, analyzing degradation trends at 300K and 400K using the HSPICE MOSRA tool. Machine learning techniques, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS), are employed on datasets comprising critical parameters such as supply voltage (VDD), threshold voltage (Vth), and oxide thickness (Toxe). Experimental results reveal that smaller nodes like 32nm experience up to 11.04% threshold voltage degradation at 400K after 10,000 cycles, compared to only 2.16% for the 250nm node at 300K. ANN models achieved a Mean Squared Error (MSE) as low as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.32\times 10^{-9}$</tex> at 300K for the 32nm node, with a predictive accuracy exceeding 99%. Regression analyses demonstrate polynomial and power models achieving <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> values of 1.00 in several scenarios, effectively capturing non-linear degradation dynamics.

articleTitle: Population Nutrition-Driven Crop Recommendations: Addressing Regional Micronutrient Deficiencies for Improved Public Health
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Crop yield optimization is paramount for an agriculture-based economy such as India, particularly in rural areas, which account for 92.02% of the agricultural workforce. However rural areas suffer the most from nutritional deficiencies. The proposed work attempts to combat the malnutrition by recommending crops which not only leverages the soil conditions (N, P, K, pH) and environmental conditions (humidity, rain, temperature) but also the micronutrient deficiencies among the regional population (Sodium, Potassium, Vitamin C, Calcium, Iron, Vitamin B6, Magnesium per 100mg). A hybrid dataset combining the crop recommendation dataset and USDA nutritional values dataset was prepared and utilized Six Machine Learning models-Decision trees, Support Vector machine (SVM), Logistic regression (LR), XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), and Naive Bayes (NB)-were trained and evaluated to determine the most effective model. The Random Forest classifier demonstrates an accuracy of 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for the dataset used. The implementation of precision farming techniques optimizes crop yield production and contributes to food security and sustainable agriculture. Furthermore, the proposed work addresses the previously overlooked issue of deficiencies and recommends crops containing nutrients based on regional requirements. This approach will significantly impact agricultural produce and the holistic health of the population.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Types, Sensors, Control & Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Last decade witnessed a significant growth for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) development, marked by advancements in innovation, production, and diverse applications across various fields. UAVs are nowadays contributing significantly in various fields like in military for surveillance, reconnaissance, planning and executing attacks, in civil applications for remote sensing, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring and conservation, infrastructure inspection and maintenance, urban planning and smart cities, scientific research and meteorology and many more. The use of UAVs has also been rapidly growing in health care and emergency medical response services. Despite this huge growth very little information is available in terms of various design and development strategies available. There is even more inadequacy of available literature sources when it comes to design and implementation of UAVs in practical world. In this paper, we tried to focus on various parameters related to UAV i.e. types, various control strategies available, onboard sensors, and potential applications in different areas. Moreover, efforts have been made to significantly address the challenges and security concerns for their better and interruption free operations.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Evaluation of Energy Consumption Across Diverse Zones
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Power demand is increasing in India day by day. The growth in power demand typically refers to the increasing need for electricity due to various factors, including population growth, economic development, urbanization, and technological advancements. Optimizing efficiency is the key to lowering the use of energy. In this paper, the authors designed a feed-forward neural network model for the evaluation of energy consumption across three zones employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm. The mean square error (MSE) and R- R-squared (R2) values were evaluated for training, testing, and validation datasets. For the training set, 427336.57 was observed as MSE and 0.9919 as the R2 value. The Mu plot was plotted. Mu is a damping factor that controls the trade-off between the gradient descent and the Gauss-Newton algorithm. It is crucial for energy planning and infrastructure development to meet future energy needs sustainably.

articleTitle: RADAR: Robust Anomaly Detection and Recognition for IoT Botnet Attacks Using Hyper-Dimensional Models
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As our world continues to embrace digital technology, cyber threats have become increasingly prevalent, especially botnet attacks. Ensuring cybersecurity is a significant concern, and to address this, we need Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) that can automatically adapt to new threats using advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. Our project aims to develop an advanced anomaly detection and recognition system for IoT botnet attacks using hyper-dimensional models namely Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and makes uses of hyperparameter tuning for performance optimization. By integrating an ensemble voting classifier that combines these five algorithms using a soft-voting mechanism, our results indicate an improved detection accuracy and adaptability. The proposed ensemble-based model is tested on a publicly available dataset which offers comprehensive coverage of botnet attack patterns and outperforms all individual classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 99.88% and an ROC AUC score of 0.999. The proposed approach highlights the advantages of combining hyper-dimensional classification models in effectively detecting IoT botnet attacks.

articleTitle: A Quantum-Enhanced Semantic Communication Framework for Securing Military Health IoT Data
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The secure Medical Internet of Things (IoT) is revolutionizing patient monitoring and healthcare data man-agement in military environments, where real-time health as-sessments of soldiers are critical. However, the exchange of sensitive medical data in these interconnected systems raises concerns about data security and privacy, particularly in military operations. This paper proposes a Quantum-Enhanced Seman-tic Communication framework to secure medical IoTin such contexts. Combining quantum communication with semantic interoperability, the framework leverages quantum mechanics principles such as entanglement and superposition to enable encryption and decryption that are resistant to conventional and emerging cyber threats. This research comprehensively analyzes quantum key distribution protocols and semantic interoperability standards to create a robust solution for secure medical data exchange in military IoTnetworks. The framework is tested with health monitoring sensors that transmit semantically rich data, protected by quantum encryption, in a simulated military environment. As quantum computing evolves, this approach offers a path to safeguard sensitive medical information in military settings, improving data security and improving the efficiency of healthcare services for soldiers.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Snoring and Non-Snoring Sound Signals Based on Singular Superlet Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for automated classification of snoring and non-snoring sound signals. The snoring and non-snoring sound signals have been represented using time-frequency representations (TFRs) obtained from singular superlet transform (SST). The obtained TFRs have been given as an input to various machine learning based classifiers, like convolutional neural network (CNN), visual geometry group 16-layer network (VGG-16), EfficientNet-B0, and hybrid VGG-16 models for the classification of snoring and non-snoring sound signals. From the experimental study, it has been observed that the hybrid VGG-16 with support vector machine (SVM) model has provided best performance among all the studied models with an accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, F1-score, and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.00%, 95.60%, 96.40%, 0.9602, 95.63%, and 0.9200 respectively. The good performance measures in automated classification of snoring and non-snoring sound signals show the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method finds applications in the area of sleep disorder diagnosis and it is suitable for real-time implementation.

Author Keywords: Classification of snoring and non-snoring sound signals

articleTitle: A Scalable Framework for IoT Applications in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The exponential growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has introduced significant challenges in managing scalability, availability, and efficiency. With billions of interconnected devices generating vast amounts of data, traditional frameworks struggle to handle the complex requirements of modern IoT applications. Addressing these challenges is crucial to fully leverage the potential of IoT in various domains, including smart homes, healthcare, and industrial automation. This paper proposes a novel framework for integrating IoT applications with cloud environments to achieve scalability and high availability. The framework is structured into four layers: the device layer leverages Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) as a low overhead communication protocol;the edge gateway layer aggregates data using lightweight Kubernetes; the ingestion and cloud infrastructure layer employs Kafka and Apache Spark for ingesting data and data transformation; and the data processing and analytics layer utilizes the cloud infrastructure layer to send the data to databases for data visualization. By leveraging cloud environments, this solution enhances scalability, availability, and overall system robustness. This paper also explores the challenges involved in implementing such an architecture, and provides insights into future advancements in IoT cloud integration.

articleTitle: Hash Based Message Authentication Code Performance with Different Secure Hash Functions
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) is a widely used cryptographic algorithm that combines a hash function with a secret key to ensure the integrity and authenticity of data. The performance of HMAC relies on the underlying hash function. In the past, Message Digest - 5 (MD5) and Secure Hash Algorithm - 1 (SHA-1) were commonly used for HMAC, but due to exponential increase of computational power, both MD5 and SHA-1 are no more secure. Consequently, Secure Hash Algorithm - 2 (SHA2-256, SHA2-384, SHA2-512) and Secure Hash Algorithm -3 (SHA3) are recommended. In these, SHA2-256 are mostly used in high end applications viz. Bitcoin, Blockchain, Smart Communication, Transport Layer Security (TLS) etc. However, understanding the quantum computation power, SHA2-512 and SHA3-512 shall be used and also it will be match the security level of AES-256. Therefore, in this paper present the comprhensive performance of the HMAC with SHA2-256, SHA2-512 and SHA3-512 with input message sizes ranging from 1 KB to 1 GB on three different platforms viz. intel i7 processor running Ubuntu and Windows, and resource-constrained Raspberry Pi 4B system. The analysis shows that SHA2-512 is significantly more efficient than SHA2-256 and SHA3-512 across all platforms and obviously provide double security than SHA2-256 which is mostly used. The experimental analysis shows that SHA2-512 processes 1 GB of data ~70% faster than SHA2-256 in i7 processors and ~90% faster on resource-constrained devices like Raspberry Pi. Hence, SHA2-512 shall be used in HMAC or in any other application which demands huge power for the systems e.g., Bitcoin or other blockchain which basically demands high security and efficient hash function. The findings show the potential of SHA2-512 and needs to replace SHA-256 in HMAC or any other applications/systems which uses hash functions.

articleTitle: V2I Communication Coverage Analysis for VANET: A Case Study for City of Bengaluru, India
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study addresses the crucial problem of maximizing Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) in metropolitan locations. For real-time data exchange to be possible in smart city applications such as traffic control, accident response, and emissions reduction, reliable V2I connection is necessary. However, maintaining reliable service in crowded urban areas is extremely difficult. This study uses the Veins framework in conjunction with the OMNeT++ simulation environment to assess Roadside Unit (RSU) deployment methodologies. Several designs are examined, with transmission ranges ranging from 100 to 500 meters, and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used to optimize placements. To evaluate the effect of RSU placement on V2I communication performance, the simulations concentrated on measures including latency, packet delivery ratio, and network connectivity. analyzing data such packet delivery ratio, latency, and overall network connectivity. The findings show that certain RSU designs greatly lower communication latency and improve packet delivery reliability, illustrating how well-placed RSUs can boost traffic control, vehicle rerouting effectiveness, and possibly lower emissions. Important insights on RSU deployment approaches are offered by this study, which additionally provides valuable recommendations for the planning of urban VANET infrastructure in Bengaluru and other comparable cities.

articleTitle: An Integrated Framework for Fake Review Detection and Review Summarization on Product Reviews
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The transformation in shopping culture from traditional markets to online markets has altered the purchasing behavior of customers with the assistance of online reviews. Nonetheless, the credibility of these reviews has been compromised by the existence of fraudulent reviews, resulting in poor buying decisions. The proposed work improves the credibility of reviews given on the internet and enhances the shopping experience of the consumers as they are able to use summarized reviews to make immediate decisions on the products. It presents a machine learning approach that tackles this problem by combining Fake Review Detection and Text Summarization as an effective information system. Uniquely, the proposed framework employs various criteria ranging from content, behavior, and length of the review to help provide a verdict that separates genuine and fraudulent reviews. Furthermore, intelligent techniques are incorporated to present reviews in short form but contains all the central and significant aspects of the review and all other details are omitted. The Bi-LSTM network for fake review detection achieved an accuracy of 94.1%, while the review summarization employs a pretrained T5-small model and a BLEU score of 0.64 is attained.

articleTitle: Altered Attentional Network Dynamics in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: A MEG-Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (TLE) is associated with widespread disruptions in brain network dynamics, affecting both cognitive and sensory processing. This study investigates the dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) of eight resting-state networks in TLE patients and Healthy Controls (HC). Network counts and dwell time, were analyzed across frequency bands to identify network-specific alterations. Results revealed that the DAN exhibited the most pronounced disruptions in TLE, with significantly higher network counts and prolonged dwell times across multiple frequency bands, reflecting compensatory mechanisms for attentional control deficits. In contrast, the VN showed reduced engagement and shorter dwell times in lower frequency bands, suggesting impaired visual processing. Other networks, such as the DMN and SMN, displayed selective alterations, highlighting their differential roles in cognitive and sensorimotor integration. These findings underscore the importance of frequency-specific dFC analyses in understanding the neural mechanisms underlying TLE- related impairments. The study highlights the potential of dFC metrics as biomarkers for identifying network disruptions and guiding targeted therapeutic interventions in epilepsy.

articleTitle: Neurological Responses to Meditation with EEG Analysis Using Novel Empirical Fourier-Bessel Decomposition Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Meditation is known for its positive impact on well-being. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals have been studied in the literature to analyze these effects. Due to the non-stationary nature of EEG signals, Fourier transform-based methods are not suitable for extracting brain patterns. Thus, analyzing and detecting changes in brain patterns associated with the progression of meditation effects become challenging. To address them, we propose a novel method, empirical Fourier-Bessel decomposition (EFBD), which combines Fourier-Bessel series expansion with an adaptive zero-phase filter bank to extract meaningful modes.
