This study has used EEG signals from 23 participants during listening to the Rudram mantra (RM) using 10-channel electrodes. To investigate significant features, energy across rhythms (delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma) has been computed from EFBD-based decomposed modes. Further, a detailed assessment of brain responses of subjects has been performed using time-frequency distribution (TFD) and topographical maps before, during, and after listening to RM. In the analysis, the band energy in the delta, theta, and alpha rhythms increased significantly after listening to the RM, which indicates enhanced relaxation, improved concentration, and reduced anxiety. It is also validated using brain region-specific analysis with TFD and topographical maps, showing increased activity in the frontal and temporal brain regions. The proposed method can be an effective tool to analyze the impact of meditation on mental health issues for individual practice.

articleTitle: Predicting Daily Rainfall Amount Using Random Forest, Multivariate Linear Regression, and Extreme Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: To utilize water resources optimally, plan agricultural activities properly, and manage the risks of natural disasters in a country such as India where the economy relies heavily on the monsoon rains, accurate rainfall prediction on a day-to-day basis becomes very crucial. This work considers rainfall prediction of several regions in India and conduct a comparative evaluation of three machine learning models - Multivariate Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting. The models were built and validated based on a rich database that contained meteorological variables that correlate with rainfall. The effectiveness of these models was assessed concerning Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). It is evident from our results that the predictive capabilities of any of the models are good, however, the XGBoost model seems to shine out as the best since it had the least RMSE and MAE values even when compared to Random Forest and Multivariate Linear Regression that were quite close. This performance hierarchy indicates that such performance of XGBoost may be a result of its potential of modeling complex non-linear relationships among the variables making it appropriate for the intricate task of predicting rainfall. The results show the prospects for further improvement in rainfall prediction with the application of more sophisticated machine learning approaches, which can noticeably integrate the complex relations between the obtained data and impacts on rainfall.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Model for Kidney Stone Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Kidney stone disease affects nearly 1 in 11 Americans over their lifetime and results in >$10 Billion of healthcare costs annually. In this paper, we propose machine learning models for the prediction of kidney stone presence in urine using five parameters of single urine samples: specific gravity, pH, osmolality, conductivity and concentrations of urea and calcium. Two types of features were engineered that capture the complex interaction between urine components (Specific gravity-to-calcium ratio and Calcium-to-pH product) and their relationship with kidney stone formation. We test the models with Logistic Regression, Support Vector Classifier(SVC), Random Forest and achieve the score of 70.65%, 72.83% and 71.74%. Based on precision-recall metrics, further evaluation indicated that SVC performed the best among other models that was highest in both stands at 0.78 for precision and 0.64 for recall. This presents a demonstration of the effectiveness and importance of machine learning models in medical diagnosis, in this case useful for non-invasive prediction of kidney stones for possible prevention or treatment.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Advancing Blockchain-Based Systems to Enhance Security and Privacy in Healthcare Data Management Practices
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Blockchain technology has become a new way to deal with the problems that healthcare data management has been having for a long time, especially when it comes to security and privacy. More and more, healthcare systems need to keep private patient information safe from leaks, illegal access, and changes. Cyberattacks are becoming more likely against traditional controlled data store models. This makes blockchain's autonomous design a hopeful answer. This study looks into how blockchain-based systems might be able to make hospital data handling safer and more private. By using blockchain's main features immutability, openness, and digital security healthcare providers can make sure that data is correct, make it safe for patients to share data, and keep strict privacy controls. This essay takes a look at how healthcare data is managed now, lists the main privacy and security issues, and gives a thorough breakdown of blockchain options. The study shows through a case study how blockchain can be added to current healthcare systems. Smart contracts and consensus methods are used to make sure that data transfers are trustworthy and accountable. The study also looks at how well blockchain systems work in terms of how fast transactions happen, how well they can be scaled, and how much they cost. It also looks at how well they protect data privacy and security.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Approach to Cost-effective Management of Typhoid Fever in Children
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Typhoid fever poses a significant health concern among children, due to its potential for severe complications and high treatment costs. This paper proposes an intelligent approach to modelling the prognosis and management of paediatric typhoid infections leveraging machine learning and data analytics to optimize healthcare resources and improve patient outcomes. The dataset was sourced from hospitals in Edo State, Nigeria. The dataset comprises laboratory tests of blood samples of children, from age zero (0) to five (5) years. Six (6) attributes that exhibit the highest information gain: widal test, malaria count, monocyte, platelets, HB, eosinophils, cost of treatment respectively, were selected and ranked thus: 0.6759, 0.4936, 0.3147, 0.2843, 0.2416, 0.2127, and 0.20. Five different classification algorithms (J48_Consolidated, LMT, RepTree, MultiBoost Decision Stump) were employed. and Random Forest) and their results were compared. Performance analysis on the five (5) classifiers shows that Multiboost Decision Stump exhibited the best accuracy of 94% and least MAE of 0.0604. The finding shows that the developed model when integrated into automated disease diagnostic workflows will provide an enhanced and flexible solution for quick prognosis of typhoid fever in children in the tropics with significant cost savings with respect to hospitalization. The finding presupposes that we can enhance the efficiency of typhoid fever management while ensuring the delivery of quality care to children in resource-limited settings.

articleTitle: Developing Predictive Models and GUI for Area & Power Estimation of PISO Shift Register for FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Shift registers with Parallel-In Serial-Out (PISO) functionality are essential components in digital electronics. They ease data transmission and minimize the amount of wiring needed by converting parallel data into a serial format, and hence used in digital communications, signal processing, and data storage. The significance of these shift registers and their guiding principles is anticipated to grow as digital technology develops, highlighting the need for a thorough analysis of their design constraints. Hence, area and power being two main design constraints for digital circuits need to be estimated. These estimates can be made using current commercial tools, however doing so requires more time because full design cycles must be followed. Therefore, challenges for designers lie in accurate estimation of resource utilization and power dissipation at the early stages of designing while working under a tight deadline. This paper develops area and power estimation models for PISO shift register circuit using the curve fitting and regression technique in MATLAB. Vivado Design Suite (2014.4) is used to simulate and synthesize these circuits for various input/output (I/O) configurations targeted to Zynq-family Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) device (xc7z020clg484-1). Furthermore, a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) is developed using Python Tkinter prompting designers to enter minimum input parameters and providing quick estimates of look-up tables (LUTs), flip-flops (FFs) and total on-chip power. These values predicted using GUI are compared with those obtained using Vivado tool. Comparison results infer that estimation errors lie in a comparable range. Hence, the proposed models and GUI expedite the design process by early and accurate estimation of area and power for FPGA-based PISO shift registers.

Author Keywords: Parallel In Serial Out Shift Register

articleTitle: Next-Generation Bug Reporting: Enhancing Development with AI Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In today's Agile and DevOps-driven software development landscape, rapid and accurate bug reporting is critical. This paper presents a next-generation automation tool powered by large language models and machine learning, innovating the bug reporting process. The tool automates various phases of bug reporting, such as failure detection, severity assessment, duplicate detection, and report generation. By addressing the limitations of manual bug reporting such as inconsistency, scalability challenges, and time inefficiencies, the proposed solution enhances the software testing workflow. Initial findings demonstrate significant time savings, reduced manual errors, and improved collaboration between testers and developers. This work establishes a foundation for fully automated bug reporting, poised to accelerate software development cycles and maintain high-quality standards.

articleTitle: Smart Parking and Automation Based System as Dynamic Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Efficient management of growing urban parking demand would require smart parking systems. A dynamic approach will be presented: using IoT-enabled algorithms, predictive analytics, and processing real-time data to optimize space utilization in the parking lot and provide convenience for users while allowing for the maximum possible operational revenue. The system achieves this by utilizing IoT sensors such as ultrasonic, infrared, and magnetic field sensors to accurately detect the occupancy of parking spaces. Algorithms for sensor data aggregation preprocess and fuse the information so that it can be relied upon and, as a result, allows for real-time monitoring. Dynamic reservation and pricing algorithms are built into the system that balances parking fees according to real-time demand, applying techniques like surge pricing, time-based adjustments, and predictive forecasting to balance occupancy and maximize revenue. Predictive analytics further supports demand forecasting by using historical data, user behavior, and environmental factors, allowing for advanced resource allocation and proactive price adjustment during peak hours. Further enhancements are added to the system in the form of edge and corner detection techniques for better vehicle identification and reservation management. The dynamic capabilities of the proposed system enhance the efficiency of operation, improve the user experience by allowing real-time spot allocation and reservations, and reduce parking congestion.

articleTitle: Progressive Use of IoT and 5G Network-Based Systems Post COVID-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The outbreak of COVID-19 has led to a reduction in a number of services and activities, but it has also accelerated the development of communication and connectivity technologies as well as touchless technology to reduce human interaction. When compared to the previous ten years, it has caused a significant technological shift in practically every sector of society, including the medical and healthcare industries, which has resulted in a restructuring of society. Automated systems and electronic devices have evolved globally with cutting-edge technologies that help to minimize the loss caused by the pandemic situation as digitalization will continue to expand. Various devices provide promising performance and are effective in maintaining physical distancing among the people. IoT and 5G network-based systems are the main concepts used in the current review to address the CoV-19 pandemic and its aftermath, with regard to accurate early detection and diagnosis, rapid, targeted treatment, and prevention of similar infection spread in the future. Adopting intelligent digitization will help address the pandemic scenario, which will lead to the creation of new methods and technologies to successfully eradicate any epidemic condition in future.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of GSSMM and EISPA in Mobile Edge Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The rapid advancements in wireless communication result in demand for low-latency and energy-efficient services. Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) offers a promising solution by providing computational resources closer to end users, thus enhancing user experience and reducing the energy consumption of mobile devices. This paper uses a novel simulation environment to deploy and evaluate the Edge-Intelligent Service Placement Algorithm (EISPA). The parameter setting used in implementation demonstrates significant energy savings for EISPA, which reduces energy consumption by 41.07% compared to Gale-Shapley Stable Marriage Matching (GSSMM). The comparative analysis also highlights EISPA's ability to handle dynamic service demands effectively. Furthermore, the results reveal the robustness of EISPA in adapting to varying network conditions, ensuring reliable service placement decisions.

articleTitle: Geneto-Neuro-Fuzzy Solution for Detection of Early Prostate Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid diagnostic model for early-stage prostate cancer, integrating genetic algorithms, neuro-fuzzy logic, and mobile agent technology. By optimizing the selection of key genetic markers, the system achieves a marked improvement in sensitivity and specificity-up to a 12% increase over conventional diagnostic methods-based on extensive simulations and a controlled clinical dataset. The neuro-fuzzy component adaptively merges genetic, clinical, and historical patient data, refining its predictive accuracy through continuous learning. A decentralized computation strategy enhances scalability and lowers device-level computational overhead, supporting widespread implementation in diverse healthcare environments. While initial results underscore its promise, validation through large-scale clinical trials remains a priority. This approach offers a practical, high-accuracy solution that could significantly reduce late-stage prostate cancer diagnoses, particularly in resourcelimited settings, and stands as a step forward in precision oncology diagnostics. The developed approach can be helpful in diagnosis of the relevant healthcare problem.

articleTitle: Optimizing Brain Tumor Classification Using YOLOv8: A Comparative Study with CNN Architectures on MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of brain tumors is crucial for effective treatment, and advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming this process. This study adapts You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8), a state-of-the-art deep learning model, for brain tumor classification using MRI scans across four categories: glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumors, and no tumor. Trained over 20 epochs with preprocessing techniques like resizing and normalization, YOLOv8 achieved a top-1 accuracy of 99.12%, outperforming traditional CNNs (94-96% accuracy). The model demonstrated faster inference, superior generalization, and consistent reductions in training and validation loss, underscoring its robustness. These results position YOLOv8 as a promising tool for early, precise, and automated tumor diagnosis, with potential for clinical deployment. Future work will focus on dataset expansion and further optimization to enhance real-world applicability

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Techniques for Face Mask Detection System in Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In high-security environments, such as the workers of a nuclear power plant, face mask detection has become extremely important in order to ensure safety and lower risks of contamination. This paper discusses the development and implementation of deep learning models with image data for detecting face masks in a nuclear power plant setting. We compare three models of great influence: CNNs, ANNs, and FNNs. All these models are trained on a large image dataset consisting of people with and without masks under various conditions of lighting and angle. This CNN-based model is known for efficiency in the field of image recognition because it has carried out several convolutional and pooling operations; it captures facial features, which results in high precision in mask detection. There are ANN and FNN models integrated in this model because its ability to optimize on the image data is less, so the comparison is done with the developed model in terms of computational tradeoff with detection performance here. Several data augmentation techniques have been made use of for noise robustness and generalization strength. Accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl score were the metrics used for the evaluation of the model performance. Conclusion it can be understood from the results obtained that with respect to accurate detection, the CNN model outperformed the ANN and FNN models. As a result, the model is quite well suited for real-time face mask detection in nuclear power plants and other similar critical infrastructures. The discovery in the safety enhancement protocols in risky environments especially shows the possibility of applying deep learning effectively for those environments.

articleTitle: Advances in Negative Capacitance FinFET Technology: Insights into Design Innovations and Performance Enhancements
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Because of their improved electrostatic control and lower power consumption, negative capacitance FinFETs, or NC-FinFETs, have attracted a lot of interest in improving the performance of nanoscale semiconductor devices. To improve the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ON}}/\mathrm{I}_{\text{OFF}}$</tex> ratio, this article investigates the integration of gate oxide (GO) topologies within NC-FinFETs, focusing on buried Interfacial GO designs that enhance subthreshold properties. The impact of varying interfacial gate oxide thickness within NC-FinFET structures, embedding the IGO layer O.6m within the channel, improves the ON-OFF current ratio, reduces substrate leakage current, and optimizes the DIBL index. We further examined the impact of dual-k spacers and selective doping to improve capacitance matching and scalability and reviewed spacers' effect on different device configurations. With Hf02 and Air as spacers, NC-FinFET gives SS values of 56.962 mY/dec and 58.830 mV/dec, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{on}/}\mathrm{I}_{\text{off}}$</tex> ratios nearly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{8}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{7}$</tex> respectively. Different combinations of spacers have been explored. Air+SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reflected high SS among all combinations. This Review demonstrates how NC-FinFETs may significantly reduce subthreshold swings and maintain operational stability at high scaling levels, revolutionizing semiconductor design.

articleTitle: Advanced Strategies for Mitigating Anomalies in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs)
publicationTitle: 2025 10th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks are emerging as critical infrastructure components in intelligent transportation systems, enabling seamless communication between vehicles and roadside units. These vulnerabilities can compromise the safety, reliability, and efficiency of the entire network, necessitating advanced strategies for anomaly detection and mitigation. Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks have evolved as an important component of intelligent transportation systems, improving traffic safety and efficiency. However, because to their dynamic and open nature, Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks are vulnerable to a variety of security vulnerabilities, including anomalies that can interrupt normal network operations. This work focuses on a complete analysis and assessment of several anomaly detection techniques in the context of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks. Vehicular ad hoc networks allow wireless communication between automobiles and vehicle-to-infrastructure systems. The fundamental purpose of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks is to improve roadway safety, comfort, and convenience. Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks differ from ad hoc networks in several ways. However, the lack of infrastructure and centralized administration renders them vulnerable to misbehavior, posing a severe danger to many elements of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks. Given its importance, this important network requires strong security measures to maintain secure communication. The suggested technique for detecting anomalies and malicious nodes in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks improves the technique by successfully selecting verifiers to detect malicious nodes, resulting in improved network performance.
